items.t: Practice makes perfect.
items.d: Things get easier the more you try them.

items.t: Look before you leap.
items.d: Think about what could happen before you act.

items.t: Two heads are better than one.
items.d: A friend might spot an answer you missed.

items.t: Many hands make light work.
items.d: Tidying a room is easier when everyone helps.

items.t: Better late than never.
items.d: You can still make a start, even if you meant to start sooner.

items.t: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
items.d: Wait to see what happens before you count on it.

items.t: Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
items.d: Keep another plan ready in case your first one fails.

items.t: Actions speak louder than words.
items.d: Helping someone means more than just saying you will.

items.t: Every cloud has a silver lining.
items.d: Even a hard day can hold something good.

items.t: A stitch in time saves nine.
items.d: Fix a small tear now, before it gets bigger.

items.t: Haste makes waste.
items.d: When you rush, mistakes can make you do the job twice.

items.t: Out of sight, out of mind.
items.d: It's easy to forget things you don't see often.

items.t: Easy come, easy go.
items.d: Things gained quickly can disappear quickly, too.

items.t: Too many cooks spoil the broth.
items.d: A shared job can get messy when everyone tries to be in charge.

items.t: All that glitters is not gold.
items.d: Something can look fine without being as good as it seems.

items.t: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
items.d: Big jobs start small. Just take the first step.

items.t: With enough work, an iron rod can be ground into a needle.
items.d: Keep going and you can do things that seem impossible.

items.t: Sharpening the knife does not delay cutting the wood.
items.d: Getting ready well first makes the real job faster.

items.t: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once.
items.d: Seeing something yourself teaches you more than being told.

items.t: When you drink the water, remember who dug the well.
items.d: Say thank you to the people who helped you get what you have.

items.t: Three people walking together always have something to learn from each other.
items.d: Everyone knows something you don't, so you can learn from anyone.

items.t: One generation plants the trees, and the next gets the shade.
items.d: Good things you do today can help people long after.

items.t: Don't wait until you are thirsty to dig a well.
items.d: Get ready ahead of time instead of waiting until you need it.

items.t: A fall into a pit is a gain in your wit.
items.d: When you make a mistake, you get smarter for next time.

items.t: Fall down seven times, get up eight.
items.d: Failing is okay. What counts is that you keep getting back up.

items.t: Even monkeys fall from trees.
items.d: Even experts make mistakes, so don't feel bad about yours.

items.t: A frog in a well does not know the great ocean.
items.d: There is a big world outside what you know. Be curious about it.

items.t: Ten people, ten colors.
items.d: Everyone is different and likes different things, and that is good.

items.t: Even dust, when piled up, becomes a mountain.
items.d: Tiny steps every day add up to something big.

items.t: Even a stone becomes warm if you sit on it for three years.
items.d: Patience and sticking with it get results in the end.

items.t: If you are in a hurry, go the long way around.
items.d: A safe, careful way often gets you there faster than rushing.

items.t: Fortune comes to the house that laughs.
items.d: Happy, cheerful people tend to have good things come their way.

items.t: See how others act, and fix your own ways.
items.d: Notice good and bad examples, and learn from them yourself.

items.t: Haraka haraka haina baraka. Hurry, hurry has no blessing.
items.d: Rushing often spoils things. Take your time and do it well.

items.t: Pole pole ndio mwendo. Slowly, slowly is the way to go.
items.d: Steady, careful steps get you where you want to go.

items.t: Haba na haba hujaza kibaba. Little by little fills the pot.
items.d: Small bits, added up day by day, make something big.

items.t: To live a long time is to see many things.
items.d: The longer you live, the more you get to see.

items.t: A person is a person through other people.
items.d: We are shaped by our family and friends, and we need each other.

items.t: When spider webs unite, they can tie up a lion.
items.d: Small people working together can do big things.

items.t: Rain does not fall on one roof alone.
items.d: Good times and hard times touch everyone, so we should help each other.

items.t: Wisdom is like a baobab tree: no one person can wrap their arms around it.
items.d: Nobody knows everything, so we all share what we know.

items.t: Knowledge makes a person humble.
items.d: The more you learn, the more you see how much is left to learn.

items.t: One and one together can make eleven.
items.d: Two people working together can be much stronger than two alone.

items.t: Do good, and good will come back to you.
items.d: Being kind to others often makes others kind to you.

items.t: What you have learned is a handful. What you have not learned is the whole world.
items.d: There is always more to learn, so keep being curious.

items.t: Patience is the key to relief.
items.d: Waiting calmly often helps problems get solved.

items.t: The dogs bark, but the caravan moves on.
items.d: Keep going with your goal, even if some people say unkind things.

items.t: Learning when you are young is like carving in stone.
items.d: What you learn as a child stays with you for a long time.

items.t: No bad thing comes without some good.
items.d: Even a tough thing can turn out to teach you something nice.

items.t: Face bad weather with a good face.
items.d: Smile through tough days and they feel easier.

items.t: Little by little, you go far.
items.d: Slow, regular steps can take you a long way.

items.t: Tell me who you walk with, and I'll tell you who you are.
items.d: The friends you choose can change how you act, so choose kind ones.

items.t: Whoever keeps at it will reach the goal.
items.d: Keep trying and you will reach your goal.

items.t: The shrimp that falls asleep is carried off by the current.
items.d: If you stop paying attention or trying, things can pass you by.

items.t: Nobody is born knowing.
items.d: Everyone learns step by step, so it's fine to ask and try.

items.t: Measure seven times, cut once.
items.d: Check your work carefully before you do something you can't undo.

items.t: Patience and hard work will grind everything down.
items.d: Keep working steadily and even hard things get done.

items.t: Without work, you can't even pull a fish out of a pond.
items.d: Nice things usually take some effort.

items.t: Morning is wiser than evening.
items.d: A problem often seems easier after a good night's sleep.

items.t: A word is not a sparrow: once it flies out, you can't catch it.
items.d: Think before you speak, because words can't be taken back.

items.t: Better to have a hundred friends than a hundred rubles.
items.d: Friends are worth more than money.

items.t: The eyes are afraid, but the hands do it.
items.d: A big job looks hard at first, but once you start, you can do it.

items.t: Repetition is the mother of learning.
items.d: Doing something again and again helps it stick in your mind.

items.t: A good laugh and a long sleep are the best cures.
items.d: Having fun and resting well help you feel better.

items.t: People live in each other's shelter.
items.d: We all need and help one another.

items.t: Praise the young and they will flourish.
items.d: Kind encouragement helps children grow and try harder.

items.t: Better a wee bush than no shelter.
items.d: A small help is still better than nothing.

items.t: He who goes slowly goes safely and goes far.
items.d: Taking your time keeps you safe and gets you far.

items.t: He who sleeps catches no fish.
items.d: You have to be awake and active to get what you want.

items.t: Whoever finds a friend finds a treasure.
items.d: A good friend is worth more than gold.

items.t: Rome wasn't built in a day.
items.d: Great things take a long time, so be patient.

items.t: Every beginning is hard.
items.d: Starting something new feels tricky, but it gets easier.

items.t: The morning hour has gold in its mouth.
items.d: Early in the day is a good time to get things done.

items.t: Trying beats studying.
items.d: Reading about something helps, but trying it teaches the most.

items.t: No effort, no prize.
items.d: Good things come to those who work for them.

items.t: Shared sorrow is half a sorrow.
items.d: Telling a friend about a problem makes it feel lighter.

items.t: Even if the sky falls, there is a way out.
items.d: There is always a way through a tough problem.

items.t: Kind words you give come back kind.
items.d: Speak nicely to others and they will speak nicely to you.

items.t: The small pepper is the hotter one.
items.d: Small people can be strong and clever.

items.t: Starting is half the job.
items.d: Once you begin something, you are already halfway there.

items.t: A tree bends while it is young.
items.d: Good habits are easiest to learn when you are young.

items.t: One tree does not make a hill, but three trees together make a high mountain.
items.d: Working together, we can do more than alone.

items.t: If you have patience, you will have stew.
items.d: Waiting and sticking with a job brings a tasty reward.

items.t: Heavy and light loads are both carried together.
items.d: A team shares the hard jobs and the easy ones.

items.t: Not all knowledge is taught in one school.
items.d: You can learn from many people and places, not just one.

items.t: What is the most important thing in the world? It is people, it is people, it is people.
items.d: People matter more than things.

items.t: The sweet potato does not speak of its own sweetness.
items.d: Be humble. Let your good deeds speak for you.

items.t: Soft water on hard stone, it keeps hitting until it makes a hole.
items.d: Gentle but steady effort can beat even hard problems.

items.t: Little by little, the bird builds its nest.
items.d: Big things are built one small piece at a time.

items.t: Shared joy is double joy.
items.d: Good news feels even better when you share it.

items.t: He who would be a leader must be a bridge.
items.d: A good leader helps people connect and cross over.

items.t: There is no bad weather, only bad clothes.
items.d: With the right gear, you can enjoy any day outside.

items.t: The more languages you know, the more times you are a person.
items.d: Each language opens a new world of friends and ideas.

items.t: Make haste slowly.
items.d: Be quick but careful, because rushing causes mistakes.

items.t: Fortune favors the brave.
items.d: Trying something bold gives you a better chance of success.

items.t: Slow and steady wins the race.
items.d: Keep going at a steady pace and you can beat a faster but careless racer.

items.t: Great oaks from little acorns grow.
items.d: Big things start from tiny beginnings.

items.t: Birds of a feather flock together.
items.d: People who are alike tend to become friends.

items.t: The early bird catches the worm.
items.d: Getting started early gives you the best chance.

items.t: Learning is like rowing upstream. If you stop, you drift back.
items.d: Keep practicing a little every day, or you slowly forget what you learned.

items.t: No task is too hard for someone who truly cares.
items.d: If you really want something and keep trying, you can do hard things.

items.t: Keep learning as long as you live.
items.d: You are never too old to learn something new, even grandparents do.

items.t: Time shoots like an arrow, and days fly like a weaver's shuttle.
items.d: Time goes by fast, so use it well.

items.t: A melon twisted off the vine is not sweet.
items.d: Forcing things usually does not work well. Be patient.

items.t: Plant melons and you get melons. Plant beans and you get beans.
items.d: Your results often reflect the effort you put in.

items.t: Fall into a pit once and you gain a little wisdom.
items.d: When you make a mistake, you learn something for next time.

items.t: Real knowledge comes from practice.
items.d: You learn to ride a bike by riding, not just by reading about it.

items.t: A good start is half of success.
items.d: Beginning well, like planning your homework, makes finishing easier.

items.t: Those with a firm goal will finally succeed.
items.d: If you know what you want and keep going, you can reach it.

items.t: A rope can saw through wood. Dripping water can pierce stone.
items.d: Small things done again and again can do amazing things.

items.t: Nearly 1 metre of ice does not form in one cold day.
items.d: Big skills grow slowly. Keep practicing a little at a time.

items.t: Share good times and share hard times.
items.d: True friends stay together whether things are fun or tough.

items.t: A long road shows a horse's strength. Time shows a person's heart.
items.d: You learn who people really are by knowing them for a long time.

items.t: Hearing about it a hundred times is not as good as seeing it once.
items.d: Seeing something yourself teaches more than just being told.

items.t: When you drink water, think of where it comes from.
items.d: Be thankful to the people who helped you.

items.t: Studying is like climbing a mountain.
items.d: Learning takes effort, one step at a time.

items.t: Uncut jade cannot become a useful thing.
items.d: Like jade, people grow better with learning and practice.

items.t: Learn it, then use it.
items.d: Using what you learn, like math at the shop, helps it stick.

items.t: Sun Jing tied his hair to a beam so he would wake up and keep studying.
items.d: People in old stories did surprising things to stay focused on learning.

items.t: Kuang Heng cut a hole in his wall to read by his neighbor's light.
items.d: He was too poor for a lamp, but he found another way to keep studying.

items.t: The more you learn, the more you see what you do not know yet.
items.d: Learning shows how big the world is. That makes you curious.

items.t: The sword's edge comes from sharpening. Plum blossom's scent comes from bitter cold.
items.d: Hard work and tough times can bring out the best in us.

items.t: Teachers open the door. You must walk in yourself.
items.d: A teacher can show you the way, but you must do the learning.

items.t: Think three times, then act.
items.d: Stop and think before you do something big.

items.t: Three monks have no water to drink.
items.d: When too many people share a job, each waits for another and nothing gets done.

items.t: Finish today's work today.
items.d: Do not put off until tomorrow what you can finish now.

items.t: The last part of a journey is the hardest.
items.d: Going 90 km of a 100 km trip is only halfway in effort. Keep going!

items.t: General Xiang Yu broke his cooking pots and sank his boats, so no one could retreat.
items.d: The idiom means: go all in, with no turning back.

items.t: Adding feet to a drawn snake spoils the picture.
items.d: It means making something worse by adding things it does not need.

items.t: A frog at the bottom of a well sees only a small circle of sky.
items.d: It means someone who has not seen much of the world.

items.t: Three people can make a tiger seem real if they all say it is.
items.d: A rumor repeated often can seem true, so check the facts.

items.t: Mend the sheep pen after the sheep are lost.
items.d: It means fixing a problem after it happens. Fixing it earlier would be better.

items.t: Liu Bei visited the wise Zhuge Liang three times to ask for help.
items.d: The idiom shows patience and respect when asking someone for help.

items.t: King Goujian tasted a bitter gall each day to remember his goal.
items.d: The idiom means: stay strong through hard times and keep your goal.

items.t: An old man dug at two mountains with hoes and baskets, and kept going.
items.d: His family would keep digging, so the tale says big goals take patience.

items.t: The bird Jingwei carried twigs and stones to fill the sea, and kept going.
items.d: In the old tale she says she will work for millions of years.

items.t: Che Yin read by the light of fireflies caught in a silk bag.
items.d: The old story says he loved books so much he found light in tiny insects.

items.t: Li Mi hung a book on his ox's horn so he could read while herding.
items.d: The story shows how he used every spare moment to learn.

items.t: Even rivals will help each other when they share a boat in a storm.
items.d: The idiom 'in the same boat' means work together when facing trouble.

items.t: Playing a lute to a cow is wasted effort.
items.d: It means talking to someone who cannot understand you, so choose your words well.

items.t: A lone hand cannot clap.
items.d: It is hard to do big things alone, so teamwork matters.

items.t: Clumsy birds fly first.
items.d: If something is harder for you, start earlier and work harder to catch up.

items.t: A hundred setbacks cannot bend you.
items.d: It means never giving up, even after many failures.

items.t: One minute on stage takes ten years of work off stage.
items.d: Great performances come from years of hidden practice.

items.t: Keeping at something builds strength.
items.d: A little practice each day can make a hard skill easier.

items.t: Patience can mean three years on a rock.
items.d: Staying patient and steady can bring good results.

items.t: Steady work can move a mountain.
items.d: A giant goal becomes possible through many small steps.

items.t: Many small strokes can bring down a large tree.
items.d: Tiny efforts add up when you keep making them.

items.t: Rising early brings a small reward.
items.d: People said an early start was worth a few small coins.

items.t: Hard times and happy times both come.
items.d: A difficult day will not last forever.

items.t: Chase two rabbits and you catch neither.
items.d: Give one important job your full attention.

items.t: A clever hawk hides its talons.
items.d: You can be skilled without showing off.

items.t: Years of living can bring wisdom.
items.d: Older people may know helpful lessons from experience.

items.t: A berry falls near its tree's roots.
items.d: People often stay connected to where they came from.

items.t: True friends become clear in hard times.
items.d: A caring friend helps when things are difficult.

items.t: A bird that leaves does not leave a mess.
items.d: Clean up your space when you finish using it.

items.t: Treasure each meeting as a special chance.
items.d: Enjoy time together because each gathering is unique.

items.t: Ten people can have ten different colors.
items.d: Everyone has their own ideas, tastes, and strengths.

items.t: Make steady progress, one step each day.
items.d: A small daily step can carry you far over time.

items.t: Two people can work in complete harmony.
items.d: Partners do well when they listen and work toward one goal.

items.t: A fair wind helps the journey go smoothly.
items.d: Good conditions can help a plan move forward.

items.t: A person watching may see the problem more clearly.
items.d: Ask someone outside the problem for a fresh view.

items.t: Bad choices often bring bad results.
items.d: Think about what your actions may cause later.

items.t: The stake that sticks up gets hammered down.
items.d: Standing out can bring criticism.

items.t: A gold coin means little to a cat.
items.d: A gift works best when the receiver can value or use it.

items.t: Choose dumplings over flowers when usefulness matters.
items.d: Something useful may matter more than something pretty.

items.t: Let a loved child go out and learn.
items.d: Trying things for yourself helps you grow.

items.t: Worrying can feel harder than doing the task.
items.d: Starting a job may show that it is easier than you imagined.

items.t: Too many captains can send a boat up a mountain.
items.d: A team works better when everyone knows who decides what.

items.t: A frog's child is still a frog.
items.d: Children often share traits with their parents.

items.t: Some things do not mix, like water and oil.
items.d: It means two things that cannot go together.

items.t: Even when you know the way, ask again.
items.d: Checking can help you notice a turn or detail you missed.

items.t: An empty cart makes the loudest rattle.
items.d: Talking loudly does not always mean knowing a lot.

items.t: One palm cannot cover the whole sky.
items.d: A small trick cannot hide a large truth.

items.t: Starting is half the task.
items.d: Once you begin, a big part of the job is already done.

items.t: Where there is determination, a road appears.
items.d: A strong goal can help you search for a way forward.

items.t: After three years at a school, even a dog can recite a poem.
items.d: Practice and repeated listening can teach surprising skills.

items.t: Plant beans and beans will grow.
items.d: The effort and choices you make shape your results.

items.t: Even rivers and mountains change in ten years.
items.d: Even huge places in nature do not stay the same.

items.t: It takes two hands to clap.
items.d: Cooperation needs people to take part together.

items.t: A tower built with care stands firm.
items.d: Careful effort creates work you can trust.

items.t: Kind words invite kind words in return.
items.d: Speaking gently can help a conversation stay friendly.

items.t: Clear water above helps keep the water below clear.
items.d: People who lead should show the good behavior they expect.

items.t: An ox has ox strength, and a bird has bird strength.
items.d: Different people are good at different things.

items.t: Do not abandon a good plan because of a small worry.
items.d: A minor problem does not have to stop the whole project.

items.t: The right match is a perfect fit.
items.d: A solution is best when it suits the exact problem.

items.t: Even a sheet of paper is easier to lift together.
items.d: Sharing a task can make it easier for everyone.

items.t: When you are in real need, a way opens.
items.d: A tight spot can still lead to a way out.

items.t: Do not scatter ashes on someone else's cooked rice.
items.d: Do not spoil another person's finished work or happy moment.

items.t: Touching one part of an elephant does not reveal the whole.
items.d: Learn about every side before deciding what something is.

items.t: While you are alive and well, the whole world is there for you.
items.d: Put your health first. Everything else you want depends on you being well.

items.t: Who sees a peacock dance deep in the forest?
items.d: A talent does not help much if nobody is there to see it. Share what you can do.

items.t: What does a monkey know about the taste of ginger?
items.d: A fine thing is wasted on someone who cannot enjoy it. Share it with a person who will.

items.t: Regret is no help once the birds have eaten the crop.
items.d: Wishing you had acted sooner does not bring the crop back. Next time, act before the loss.

items.t: If you cannot dance, do not blame the bumpy yard.
items.d: When something goes badly, it is easy to blame the tools. First check your own skill.

items.t: Distant drums sound nicer than drums close by.
items.d: Other people's lives can look better from far away. Up close, everyone has hard bits.

items.t: The chicken at home seems no better than plain lentils.
items.d: Lentils are everyday food. We often care least about good things that are easy to get.

items.t: If you live in the water, do not quarrel with the crocodile.
items.d: Do not start trouble with someone you depend on. You still share the same place.

items.t: Why use a mirror to see the bangle on your wrist?
items.d: Some things are so clear that you do not need more proof. You can already see them.

items.t: The one who did wrong scolds the person who caught him.
items.d: People sometimes blame others for a mistake that was really their own.

items.t: Drop by drop, the water pot becomes full.
items.d: Small efforts add up. Saving a little, or practicing a little, can finish a big job.

items.t: He fell from the sky and got stuck in a date palm.
items.d: Sometimes you escape one problem and fall into a worse one. Check the way out first.

items.t: One firm strike by a blacksmith beats a hundred light taps.
items.d: One clear, strong try can beat lots of tiny fussy ones. Put your effort where it counts.

items.t: Not everything white is milk.
items.d: Looks can fool you. A thing may seem good or true and still be something else.

items.t: Why hunt for honey in the hills if it is at home?
items.d: Look for what you need close by before you go on a long search.

items.t: Humility is worth a thousand gold coins.
items.d: Humility means staying modest. This saying says modesty can bring a great reward.

items.t: Keep at it, and even a heavy grinding stone will move.
items.d: A hard job can shift if you keep working. Steady tries move what feels stuck.

items.t: The beauty of the heart shows on the face.
items.d: How you feel inside often shows outside. A kind heart tends to make a kind face.

items.t: Do not step into water until you know its depth.
items.d: Look before you leap. Learn what you are getting into before you start.

items.t: Even if you pour it in the river, measure it first.
items.d: Be careful with what you have, even when there is plenty. Waste is still waste.

items.t: Ploughing deep is better than ploughing wide.
items.d: Do one job properly instead of rushing over many. A deep job beats a quick skim.

items.t: A pumpkin drawn in a book cannot be cooked for dinner.
items.d: Reading about a skill is not the same as doing it. Real work needs practice.

items.t: Even an elephant slips sometimes.
items.d: Everybody makes mistakes, even people who seem strong or sure. One slip is not the end.

items.t: The wolf cried because the sheep was getting wet.
items.d: The wolf only pretends to feel sorry for the sheep. That kind of care is not real.

items.t: Do not ask a cat to guard a pot of milk.
items.d: Do not leave the milk with a cat. Choose a helper who fits the job.

items.t: He is like a cat sitting on a wall.
items.d: A cat on a wall has not picked a side. This is said about someone who cannot decide.

items.t: He looks for ghee while butter is already in his hand.
items.d: Ghee is a butter you cook with. He already holds it, yet he keeps searching. Look first.

items.t: Ask him for sesame seeds, and he is ready with the oil.
items.d: He thinks one step ahead. He is ready for the next need before you even ask.

items.t: It is like tying a silk tassel on a broom.
items.d: A silk bow on a broom does not make the broom special. A fancy cover leaves it a broom.

items.t: Miss a white cow by day, and you will miss a buffalo at night.
items.d: If you cannot manage an easy task, a harder one will be even tougher.

items.t: With the five and the three basics ready, even a new cook can start.
items.d: Pepper, salt, mustard, cumin, tamarind, water, fire, and fuel are enough to begin cooking.

items.t: Even hot water will still put out a fire.
items.d: The saying means a thing keeps its true nature, even if it seems a little changed.

items.t: A pot full of water stays quiet when you shake it.
items.d: People who know a lot often speak less. People who know little often talk the most.

items.t: To the loris, her own baby is a precious gem.
items.d: A loris is a small night animal. What looks plain to you may be treasure to someone else.

items.t: Rush, and you cannot even slip a hand into the pot.
items.d: Hurrying makes you miss simple steps. Slow down, and the easy part gets easier.

items.t: The crane's white feathers show best when it flies off.
items.d: We often see how special something is only after it has gone. Notice it sooner.

items.t: Save the jaggery you still have, instead of crying over the lost bit.
items.d: Jaggery is a kind of sweet. After a loss, look after what is left and keep going.

items.t: Fall in a hole at night, and you will avoid it by day.
items.d: A mistake can teach you. Once you have seen the hole, you can walk around it next time.

items.t: A tree full of fruit draws every kind of creature.
items.d: When someone does well, many people want to come close. Success draws a crowd.

items.t: What goes up must come down.
items.d: This saying means a high moment does not last forever. What rises will fall again.

items.t: Water, food, and wise sayings are three jewels of the earth.
items.d: A wise saying is as precious as a meal or a drink. Shiny stones are not the real jewels.

items.t: Trees give fruit, rivers flow, and cows give milk for others.
items.d: The best gifts are shared. These words praise a life that helps other people.

items.t: Unkind words come back as unkind answers.
items.d: Speak kindly if you want a kind reply. The way you talk shapes the way people answer.

items.t: Will a tiger give birth to a cat?
items.d: Children often grow up to be like their parents. Family ways tend to show.

items.t: You cannot hide gold inside a rag.
items.d: Gold shows through a thin cloth. Real worth is hard to cover up.

items.t: You see the speck in someone else's eye, but not in your own.
items.d: It is easy to notice a small fault in others and miss that same fault in yourself.

items.t: The lotus flower blooms in the middle of the mud.
items.d: A lotus is a flower that grows in muddy water. Picture it opening up bright and clean.

items.t: If someone is chasing you, keep going. They are getting tired too.
items.d: Do not give up in a hard moment. Others are finding it hard too.

items.t: The child of an elephant will not be a dwarf.
items.d: Children often grow to share traits with their family.

items.t: Only the thing you struggle for will last.
items.d: Things you work hard for are the ones you keep and value most.

items.t: Whoever is patient with a cowrie shell will one day have thousands.
items.d: Cowries were used as money. Saving a little at a time grows into a lot.

items.t: Water may cover a footprint, but it cannot cover the words of the mouth.
items.d: Things you say stay with people. Choose your words with care.

items.t: Patience is the father of character.
items.d: Learning to wait calmly helps you become a kind and strong person.

items.t: Wisdom is better than strength.
items.d: Thinking smart can solve a problem that muscles cannot.

items.t: A child who is not taught will sell the house that was built.
items.d: Children need to be taught, so they can look after what they are given.

items.t: He who does not know the town does not know the farm.
items.d: Knowing your surroundings helps you find your way.

items.t: All fingers are not the same.
items.d: People are different, and that is fine. Each one is good in their own way.

items.t: One head does not hold a council.
items.d: Big decisions are better when many people share ideas.

items.t: If a bird does not fly, it goes to bed hungry.
items.d: You have to make an effort to get what you need.

items.t: If you do not let your friend cross, you will not cross either.
items.d: When we help each other, everybody gets through.

items.t: We send a wise person, not one with long legs.
items.d: For an important job, pick someone who thinks well, not someone who is just fast.

items.t: It is when you climb a good tree that we push you.
items.d: People cheer you on and help when you are doing something good.

items.t: If one finger brings oil, it soils all the others.
items.d: One person's actions can affect the whole group. Chinua Achebe used this in a novel.

items.t: When there is a big tree, small ones climb on its back to reach the sun.
items.d: Young ones can reach higher by learning from those who are bigger and older.

items.t: A fish is a king in the water.
items.d: Everyone is strongest in the place where they belong.

items.t: One tree does not make a forest.
items.d: A group is made of many. One person alone cannot do everything.

items.t: A child who washes his hands could eat with kings.
items.d: Being clean and well-mannered opens doors for you.

items.t: The fly that follows meat does not starve.
items.d: Staying near a useful source can help you share its benefits.

items.t: The crab becomes king in a small pool of water.
items.d: Someone can look very important in a small place. Do not boast too soon.

items.t: Thoughts are like shoulder-bags: each person slings his own.
items.d: Everyone thinks in their own way. It is fine that ideas differ.

items.t: Children of the same mother are like the fingers of one hand.
items.d: Brothers and sisters belong together and work best as a team.

items.t: Whoever spends time at the well can soon find a bucket.
items.d: Be in the right place and you will meet good chances.

items.t: Soap does not do the laundry alone.
items.d: Tools help, but you still need to do some work yourself.

items.t: Every calabash bowl has its lid.
items.d: There is a good match for everyone and everything.

items.t: A person is measured by what they do, not by what they say.
items.d: Actions show who you really are.

items.t: Whatever is painful does not last. Whoever keeps going will smile.
items.d: Hard times end. If you keep trying, happy times come.

items.t: Patience can cook a stone.
items.d: Even the hardest job can be done if you are patient enough.

items.t: Dignity is like oil. Once spilled, it cannot be gathered again.
items.d: Keep your good name safe, because it is hard to win back once lost.

items.t: One who often asks for directions never misses the way.
items.d: Asking questions helps you learn and keeps you from getting lost.

items.t: A child does not trip over the same doorstep twice.
items.d: Learn from your mistakes. This is a Bayangi proverb from Cameroon.

items.t: A man who has not traveled thinks his mother is the best cook in the world.
items.d: Seeing new places teaches you more. This is a Bakossi proverb from Cameroon.

items.t: A small problem that is ignored will grow big.
items.d: Fix little troubles early, before they get bigger. This is a Bayangi proverb.

items.t: Walls have ears.
items.d: Be careful what you say, because others may be listening. This is a Medumba proverb from Cameroon.

items.t: A flea can trouble a lion more than a lion can trouble a flea.
items.d: Even small ones can bother the big and strong. Medumba proverb, Cameroon.

items.t: Whoever seeks will find.
items.d: If you keep looking and trying, you will find what you need. Medumba proverb, Cameroon.

items.t: There is no long road without corners.
items.d: Every long journey has turns and surprises. Medumba proverb, Cameroon.

items.t: Whoever goes slowly goes surely.
items.d: Taking your time can be the safest way to get there. Medumba proverb, Cameroon.

items.t: A clear conscience is a soft mat.
items.d: Doing what is right helps your mind rest easily.

items.t: Follow bees so that you may eat honey.
items.d: Learn from those who know the way to a good result.

items.t: Hurry, hurry, has no blessings.
items.d: Rushing can lead to mistakes. Take time to do things well.

items.t: Kindness does not go bad.
items.d: A kind deed keeps its value long after you do it.

items.t: Do not set sail using somebody else's star.
items.d: Choose your own goal instead of copying another person's path.

items.t: One does not become great by claiming greatness.
items.d: What you do matters more than what you say about yourself.

items.t: Love does not choose the blade of grass on which it falls.
items.d: Friendship and care can grow in unexpected places.

items.t: There is no homestead where smoke does not rise.
items.d: Every family has some problems to solve.

items.t: The bull is in the calves.
items.d: Young people carry the strength and promise of the future.

items.t: The small pot is like the big one.
items.d: Children often learn habits and ways of doing things from adults.

items.t: The way you bring up a child is the way the child grows.
items.d: Patient teaching and good examples help children grow well.

items.t: When elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers.
items.d: A quarrel between powerful people can trouble others nearby.

items.t: Eating without sharing is like swearing with your mouth.
items.d: When you have enough, sharing is a caring choice.

items.t: To give away is to make provision for the future.
items.d: Generosity builds friendships and support for days ahead.

items.t: The one who offended forgets, but the one who suffered remembers.
items.d: Your words may affect someone longer than you realize.

items.t: To travel is to see.
items.d: Visiting new places helps you see and learn new things.

items.t: People know each other better on a journey.
items.d: Shared experiences reveal how people think, help, and solve problems.

items.t: Old people sit in shade because they planted a tree long ago.
items.d: Work done today can help you and others far into the future.

items.t: A crowd is bad for eating, but good for work.
items.d: A group may use more supplies, but many helpers can finish a big job.

items.t: One who uses both hands cannot fail to eat.
items.d: Careful, complete effort helps you meet your needs.

items.t: One who sees something good must tell about it.
items.d: Share useful discoveries so that others can learn too.

items.t: A bird builds its nest with feathers from other birds.
items.d: We often create good things with help from other people.

items.t: Little pots have ears.
items.d: Children may hear adult conversations, so speak with care around them.

items.t: A monkey that cannot reach ripe bananas says they are not ripe.
items.d: Sometimes people pretend something is bad only because they cannot get it.

items.t: One stick at a time makes a bundle.
items.d: Small steps add up to something large and useful.

items.t: What ripens quickly, rots quickly.
items.d: Fast results may not last. Strong work often takes time.

items.t: If you laugh at the bowl, you laugh at the potter.
items.d: Before mocking something, remember the effort and skill used to make it.

items.t: One who has not travelled thinks their mother is the world's best cook.
items.d: New experiences show us that there are many good ways to do things.

items.t: To try and fail is not laziness.
items.d: An honest attempt still shows effort, even when it does not work.

items.t: Life is full of banana skins. You slip, you carry on.
items.d: Mistakes and setbacks happen. Get up, learn, and keep going.

items.t: An old banana leaf was once young and green.
items.d: Every older person was once young, just as every child will grow older.

items.t: A small gift strengthens a friendship.
items.d: A simple, thoughtful act can show a friend that you care.

items.t: People are wealth.
items.d: Caring relationships can be more valuable than things or money.

items.t: Virtue is better than riches.
items.d: Being honest and kind matters more than owning many things.

items.t: Wealth comes by cultivating together.
items.d: People can achieve more when they work as a team.

items.t: There is no rain that does not bring wealth to someone.
items.d: Rain can bring wealth to someone, like water for a farmer's crops.

items.t: Steadiness makes wealth.
items.d: Regular effort over time can build something valuable.

items.t: Peace is costly, but it is worth the expense.
items.d: Making peace can take patience and effort, but the result is valuable.

items.t: Do not hurry the night. The sun will always rise for its own sake.
items.d: Some things cannot be rushed. Be patient while you wait.

items.t: Fire is not put out with fire.
items.d: Anger usually does not solve anger. A calm response can help.

items.t: Nobody is born wise.
items.d: Wisdom grows through learning, listening, and experience.

items.t: A word once said cannot be taken back.
items.d: Pause before speaking because words can stay in another person's mind.

items.t: The sound of the drum depends on the drummer.
items.d: The result often depends on the care and skill of the person doing the work.

items.t: Never throw away the old at the sight of the new.
items.d: Do not forget something useful just because something newer appears.

items.t: Where there is negotiation, there is hope for agreement.
items.d: Talking and listening can help people find an answer together.

items.t: To be without friends is to be truly poor.
items.d: Good friends add a kind of richness that money cannot buy.

items.t: A nice word is better than a nice mattress.
items.d: Kind words can bring comfort that even a soft bed cannot give.

items.t: Rice is one thing, but there are many ways of cooking it.
items.d: Different methods can all lead to a good result.

items.t: One head does not hold all knowledge.
items.d: No one knows everything. We learn more by listening to one another.

items.t: If you never ask questions, you never learn.
items.d: Curiosity starts with a question. If you never ask, the answer stays hidden.

items.t: While you are on your feet, help someone who has fallen.
items.d: If you are doing fine, lend a hand to a friend who is having a hard time.

items.t: A drop becomes an ocean only when it joins the ocean.
items.d: One drop is tiny. Joined with many others, it becomes something huge.

items.t: With time and skill, a mulberry leaf becomes satin.
items.d: Patience and skill can turn something simple into something fine and smooth.

items.t: Mountains never meet, but people do.
items.d: Friends may live far apart, yet they can still find each other again.

items.t: A lazy sheep thinks its own wool is heavy.
items.d: When you do not feel like working, even a small job can seem huge.

items.t: When he finally decided to go to school, it was the weekend.
items.d: This funny Persian saying is about Hasani. Wait too long, and the chance can pass.

items.t: Nothing is cheap for no reason.
items.d: A very low price can hide a problem. Pause and look before you grab it.

items.t: The neighbor's chicken looks like a goose.
items.d: Someone else's things can seem better than yours, even when they are not.

items.t: You cannot hold two watermelons in one hand.
items.d: Pick one big job at a time. If it is too much, ask someone to help.

items.t: The one who seeks is the one who finds.
items.d: If you never search or try, you will not discover what you hoped for.

items.t: Not every round thing is a walnut.
items.d: Looks can fool you. Check before you decide something is the real prize.

items.t: Saying 'halva' does not make your mouth sweet.
items.d: Halva is a sweet food. Wishing out loud will not put that taste on your tongue.

items.t: Bake the bread while the oven is still hot.
items.d: Do the job when the moment is right. A cold oven will not bake the loaf.

items.t: Is money just leaves to a bear?
items.d: No. Money does not grow on trees. Someone has to earn it.

items.t: They ate the salt, then broke the salt shaker.
items.d: Do not take someone's kindness and then turn against them.

items.t: Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.
items.d: Waiting can feel hard now. Later, that patience can bring a happy result.

items.t: One try will not bring a big tree down.
items.d: Big goals need many tries. Keep at it, a little at a time.

items.t: Not knowing is no shame. Refusing to learn is.
items.d: It is fine to say you do not know yet. Then take the next step and learn.

items.t: Everyone is the blacksmith of their own star.
items.d: A blacksmith shapes metal. You, too, can shape the kind of future you want.

items.t: A good start is already half the job.
items.d: Begin with care, and the rest of the work gets much easier.

items.t: A barking dog seldom bites.
items.d: Loud fuss is often just noise. It does not always turn into action.

items.t: Never felt the sun? You may not value the shade.
items.d: A cool rest feels best when you know what the heat was like.

items.t: The pear falls close to its tree.
items.d: Kids often grow up sharing habits with the family around them.

items.t: Out of sight can mean out of the heart.
items.d: If you never see a friend, you may forget them. Send a hello and stay close.

items.t: Rush a job, and mistakes rush in with it.
items.d: Slow down a little. Careful work usually comes out better.

items.t: Drop by drop, a pond can form.
items.d: Small saves, practice, or kind acts add up to something big.

items.t: Bend the tree while it is still young.
items.d: A green branch bends with ease. Good habits are easier to start early too.

items.t: One hard lesson beats a thousand lectures.
items.d: Living through something can teach you more than only being told about it.

items.t: One blossom does not make a summer.
items.d: One example is not a whole pattern. Wait and see what happens next.

items.t: Iron that is used does not grow rusty.
items.d: Keep practicing a skill so it stays sharp, like a busy tool that stays bright.

items.t: Whoever rises early gets a head start.
items.d: Begin sooner, and you have more calm time to do the job well.

items.t: One hand is quiet. Two hands can clap.
items.d: Working together gets more done than trying to do it all alone.

items.t: A true friend shows up on a hard day.
items.d: Real friends come when you need them, not only when things are easy.

items.t: Do not laugh at your neighbor's bad luck.
items.d: Be kind when someone else has trouble. One day you may want that kindness.

items.t: Sweet words can bring a snake out of its hole.
items.d: Speaking kindly can calm someone and help them come closer to you.

items.t: After hot milk, you blow on yogurt too.
items.d: One surprise makes you careful next time, even when things are probably fine.

items.t: Be stricter with yourself than with others.
items.d: Before you point at a friend's mistake, look at your own with extra care.

items.t: Stretch your feet only as far as the blanket.
items.d: Use what you really have. Do not plan to spend more than you can cover.

items.t: Save the hay. A day for it will come.
items.d: Keep useful odds and ends. A small thing you saved may help later.

items.t: A small gift from the heart can match a large one.
items.d: The kindness in a gift matters more than how big or costly it is.

items.t: Without the work, there is no food.
items.d: The food you eat took work. Good results usually need effort first.

items.t: You harvest what you plant.
items.d: What you do comes back to you. Kind work tends to bring kind results.

items.t: The rope of a lie is short.
items.d: A lie can stretch only so far. Sooner or later, the truth shows.

items.t: Everyone who falls has someone to catch them.
items.d: If you slip, you are not alone. A friend can be there to help you up.

items.t: Too many herders, and the sheep get lost.
items.d: When too many people give orders at once, nobody knows what to do.

items.t: Do not call it wheat until it is harvested.
items.d: Wait until a plan truly succeeds before you cheer and count the prize.

items.t: I know the sun of my own country best.
items.d: The place you live every day is the one you understand most clearly.

items.t: “A la tercera va la vencida”
items.d: Another try may succeed, so do not give up after two tries.

items.t: “Árbol que nace torcido, jamás su tronco endereza”
items.d: Early habits can be hard to change, so choose good ones from the start.

items.t: “A falta de pan, buenas son tortas”
items.d: If you can't have the best thing, be happy with what you have.

items.t: “A donde fueres, haz lo que vieres”
items.d: When you visit a new place, follow how people do things there.

items.t: “Apretados pero contentos”
items.d: A squeezed-in group can still be happy. The more friends, the more fun.

items.t: “Bien predica quien bien vive”
items.d: Show good behavior yourself. People learn more from what you do than from what you say.

items.t: “Buen yunque no teme el martillo”
items.d: If you are strong and sure of yourself, hard knocks do not scare you.

items.t: “Cada oveja, con su pareja”
items.d: Friends often match: people who are alike tend to hang out together.

items.t: “Cuando una puerta se cierra, ciento se abren”
items.d: When one chance ends, many new ones can begin.

items.t: “Cuídame del agua mansa”
items.d: Calm, quiet water can be deep. Quiet people may know and feel a lot.

items.t: “Del mal el menos”
items.d: When every choice is hard, pick the one with the smallest problem.

items.t: “La unión hace la fuerza”
items.d: Together we are stronger than alone.

items.t: “Las apariencias engañan”
items.d: Looks can fool you. Get to know something before you judge it.

items.t: “Lo barato cuesta caro”
items.d: Something very cheap may break fast, so you pay more in the end.

items.t: “Los grandes ingenios se encuentran”
items.d: Smart people often come up with the same idea.

items.t: “Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando”
items.d: A sure thing can be better than many things you may never get.

items.t: “Más vale un hecho que cien palabras”
items.d: One thing you do counts more than a hundred things you say.

items.t: “Más vale tarde que nunca”
items.d: Doing something late is better than never doing it.

items.t: “Mejor es doblar que quebrar”
items.d: Be flexible. A bending branch survives wind that snaps a stiff one.

items.t: “Mirar antes de saltar”
items.d: Think and check before you do something big.

items.t: “Muchos golpes derriban un roble”
items.d: Many small hits can bring down a big oak tree. Keep going bit by bit.

items.t: “Nadie es indispensable”
items.d: Nobody is the only one who can do a job. Everyone can learn and share.

items.t: “No dejes para mañana lo que puedas hacer hoy”
items.d: If you can do it today, do it now and don't put it off.

items.t: “Echar margaritas a puercos”
items.d: Don't give something precious to someone who won't care about it.

items.t: “El hilo siempre se rompe por lo más delgado”
items.d: A thread snaps where it is thinnest. Look after the weak spots.

items.t: “El perro ladra y la caravana pasa”
items.d: Keep going on your path, even when others bark with complaints.

items.t: “El poeta nace, el orador se hace”
items.d: Some talents come naturally, but speaking well is learned by practice.

items.t: “En boca cerrada ni moscas ni nada”
items.d: Keeping quiet at the right time can save you from trouble.

items.t: “En casa del herrero, cuchillo de palo”
items.d: People may be skilled at helping others but neglect the same needs at home.

items.t: “Hacer de una pulga un elefante”
items.d: Don't turn a tiny problem into a giant one.

items.t: “Hombre prevenido vale por dos”
items.d: Knowing what may happen helps you get ready for it.

items.t: “El tiempo y la marea no esperan al rey”
items.d: Time and tides wait for nobody, not even a king.

items.t: “En la variedad está el gusto”
items.d: Different things make life fun. Variety adds flavor.

items.t: “Fue por lana y salió trasquilado”
items.d: He went to get wool and came back with a haircut. Plans can backfire.

items.t: “A caballo regalado no se le mira el diente”
items.d: Be thankful for gifts. Do not check a present for flaws.

items.t: “A lo hecho, pecho”
items.d: What is done is done. Face it bravely and move on.

items.t: “Al mentiroso le conviene ser memorioso”
items.d: A liar needs a great memory to keep the stories straight. Tell the truth.

items.t: “Al hombre osado la fortuna le da la mano”
items.d: Being bold enough to try can open new chances.

items.t: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
items.d: When someone gives you a gift, be thankful instead of hunting for faults.

items.t: After rain comes sunshine.
items.d: A hard or gloomy time can be followed by a happier one.

items.t: As you make your bed, so you must lie.
items.d: Your choices often shape what happens next, so choose with care.

items.t: When in doubt, do not do it.
items.d: If you are not sure a choice is wise, it is safer to wait.

items.t: Do not make an elephant out of a fly.
items.d: Try not to turn a small problem into a huge one.

items.t: A fault confessed is half forgiven.
items.d: Saying you were wrong is a big step toward being forgiven.

items.t: Strike while the iron is hot.
items.d: When a good chance arrives, act before the chance passes.

items.t: To eat the kernel, you must crack the nut.
items.d: A worthwhile reward often takes effort to reach.

items.t: Do not wake a sleeping cat.
items.d: Do not restart an old problem that has already become quiet.

items.t: Think before you act.
items.d: Think about what could happen before making a big choice.

items.t: Step back to take a good leap.
items.d: A short pause can help you prepare for better progress.

items.t: Where there's smoke, there's fire.
items.d: A clue may point to a real problem, but check the facts before deciding.

items.t: Appearances can deceive.
items.d: Something may be different from how it first looks. Learn more before judging.

items.t: Better to bend than to break.
items.d: Being flexible can help you handle change without giving up.

items.t: The grass is always greener in the neighbor's field.
items.d: Other people's lives may look better, even when you cannot see their problems.

items.t: Barking dogs seldom bite.
items.d: Someone who makes lots of noise may not be as powerful as they sound.

items.t: Constant drops wear away the stone.
items.d: Small efforts repeated many times can achieve something difficult.

items.t: To every bird, its own nest is beautiful.
items.d: Home can feel special because it is familiar and belongs to you.

items.t: A good beginning makes a good ending.
items.d: Starting with care makes it easier to finish a task well.

items.t: Love me, love my dog.
items.d: Caring about someone also means respecting what matters to them.

items.t: Do a job yourself, and it counts for three.
items.d: Your own effort can get more done than waiting for help.

items.t: Patience helps you gain knowledge.
items.d: Taking your time and staying with a task helps you learn.

items.t: A person is known by the company they keep.
items.d: The friends you choose can influence your habits and choices.

items.t: It is no use crying over spilled milk.
items.d: You cannot undo the past, but you can clean up and decide what to do next.

items.t: Better an egg today than a hen tomorrow.
items.d: A small sure thing may be wiser than waiting for a bigger uncertain reward.

items.t: Experience is the mother of knowledge.
items.d: Doing things and learning from them helps you make wiser choices.

items.t: Where there is life, there is hope.
items.d: As long as you can keep trying, there is a chance for things to improve.

items.t: Don't hear one and judge two.
items.d: Do not judge everyone after hearing only one person's story.

items.t: The donkey called the rooster bigheaded.
items.d: People sometimes criticize a fault in others while missing the same fault in themselves.

items.t: A green fruit gets ripe slowly.
items.d: Growth takes time. You do not have to master everything at once.

items.t: If you buy cheaply, you may pay dearly.
items.d: The cheapest choice can cost more later if it does not last or work well.

items.t: The walls have ears.
items.d: Speak carefully because private words may be heard or repeated.

items.t: Stones never meet, but people do.
items.d: People may cross paths again, so treat everyone with kindness.

items.t: Time is precious.
items.d: Use your time for things that matter, because spent time cannot be bought back.

items.t: We notice another's splinter but miss our own beam.
items.d: Check your own mistakes before pointing out someone else's smaller ones.

items.t: A closed mouth catches no flies.
items.d: Staying quiet can keep you from saying something careless.

items.t: Little by little, the sink and barrel fill.
items.d: Many tiny amounts can grow into something large.

items.t: An old dog does not bark in vain.
items.d: Listen when an experienced person warns you. They may notice something you missed.

items.t: Still waters run deep.
items.d: A quiet person may have many thoughtful ideas that are not obvious at first.

items.t: Run after two hares, and you catch neither.
items.d: Focusing on one task can work better than chasing two goals at once.

items.t: Don't leave for tomorrow what you can do today.
items.d: Finishing a task now keeps it from becoming a worry later.

items.t: Better a little that is fair than a lot that is unfair.
items.d: A small honest share is worth more than a big unfair one.

items.t: Many a true word is spoken in jest.
items.d: A joke can sometimes contain an honest thought worth noticing.

items.t: Good things often come in threes.
items.d: A fun day can have three happy parts, like a game, a snack, and a story.

items.t: Honor older people, and teach younger ones.
items.d: Listen when grandparents share what they know. Then help a smaller child learn too.

items.t: Everything has its right time.
items.d: Apples ripen in autumn. Waiting for the right moment can beat rushing.

items.t: Late help is better than no help.
items.d: Showing up late to help still matters more than not showing up at all.

items.t: One today is worth ten tomorrows.
items.d: Reading one page now helps more than promising to read ten pages someday.

items.t: If the ending is good, the whole thing is good.
items.d: A game can start badly and still feel great if you finish as friends.

items.t: If you rush too much, you may spoil the job.
items.d: Hurrying a drawing can make a smudge. A steady hand keeps the picture neat.

items.t: Think first, then act.
items.d: Before you jump a puddle, check how wide it is. A quick look can save a splash.

items.t: What stays out of sight may slip from your mind.
items.d: If you put a book in a closed box, you may forget it until you see it again.

items.t: Family ties can be stronger than other ties.
items.d: You may argue with a brother or sister, then still stick together afterward.

items.t: People who are alike often stick together.
items.d: Kids who love the same game tend to gather on the same part of the playground.

items.t: Shared joy grows, and a shared worry shrinks.
items.d: Telling a friend about a fun win makes it brighter. Telling a worry makes it lighter.

items.t: Little kids often have big ears.
items.d: They may hear a quiet talk nearby. Speak kindly, because they are listening.

items.t: Not everything shiny is real gold.
items.d: A plastic coin can sparkle and still be a toy. Look closer before you decide.

items.t: One swallow does not mean summer has come.
items.d: One warm afternoon does not mean the cold days are gone. Wait for the real pattern.

items.t: Do not turn against the person who helps you.
items.d: If someone shares lunch with you, thank them. Kindness should get kindness back.

items.t: A closed mouth keeps the flies out.
items.d: Staying quiet can keep you out of a silly argument. You do not have to say everything.

items.t: The apple lands close to its tree.
items.d: Children often pick up habits from their family, like a love of songs or puzzles.

items.t: You know a tree by the fruit it grows.
items.d: You know a person by what they do. Kind acts show a kind heart.

items.t: When the cat leaves, the mice start to play.
items.d: If the coach steps out, the team may get silly. People act freer without a watcher.

items.t: Even a little bit of help counts.
items.d: A few coins in a jar still add up. Small help can finish a big job.

items.t: A steady drip can wear a hole in stone.
items.d: One drop does little. The same drop, day after day, can change something hard.

items.t: Do good, and good often comes back.
items.d: If you hold a door for someone, another person may hold one for you later.

items.t: Begin well, and the ending is easier.
items.d: If you pack your bag the night before, the morning goes more smoothly.

items.t: The more friends, the merrier.
items.d: A game of tag is more fun when extra friends join in and play fairly.

items.t: Kind words work better than sharp ones.
items.d: Asking nicely gets more help than snapping. A sweet tone opens more doors.

items.t: Kids follow what you do more than what you say.
items.d: If you want a friend to tidy up, start tidying. They learn from your actions.

items.t: Someone dearly loved may have many nicknames.
items.d: Nicknames like buddy or champ show love. People give extra names to someone dear.

items.t: A good laugh makes life longer.
items.d: This is an old saying. It means laughing with friends keeps you happy and well.

items.t: Mistakes can become lessons.
items.d: A wrong answer on a quiz shows what to practice. The next try can be better.

items.t: A late start can still be a real start.
items.d: You can start learning the piano this year, even if others started earlier.

items.t: Sunshine follows the rain.
items.d: A gloomy hour can pass. A tough school day can still end with a happy walk home.

items.t: Do not keep all your eggs in a single basket.
items.d: If one plan fails, another can still work. Spread your chances a little.

items.t: A bird you hold beats ten birds on the roof.
items.d: A small prize you already have can beat a bigger prize you only hope for.

items.t: Light a candle instead of grumbling at the dark.
items.d: If a room is dim, switch on a lamp. Doing one small helpful thing beats only complaining.

items.t: When you fix a mess, keep what is still good.
items.d: If a story has one weak sentence, change that line. Do not throw away the whole story.

items.t: Crawl first, and walking comes after.
items.d: Master the small steps first. Then try the bigger ones, like a long bike ride.

items.t: Shape the iron while it is still hot.
items.d: When the moment is right, act. Start the project while you still feel ready.

items.t: An eagle does not waste time on flies.
items.d: A big goal may matter more than a tiny fuss. Save your energy for the important job.

items.t: Even a hen with poor sight may find a seed.
items.d: Keep trying at the problem. A lucky find can still come while you work.

items.t: An honest way lasts longer than a trick.
items.d: A true story stays solid. A made-up one can fall apart when questions come.

items.t: The first in line is served first.
items.d: At a busy water fountain, the person who arrives first gets a turn first.

items.t: A small fence can help friends stay friends.
items.d: Share kindly, and also respect a friend's space. A little boundary can keep peace.

items.t: Steady hard work can beat a run of bad luck.
items.d: If a plant wilts once, keep watering and learning. Effort can turn things around.

items.t: The best results often arrive slowly.
items.d: A puzzle comes together piece by piece. Patience helps the picture appear.

items.t: Do not make a huge fuss over a tiny problem.
items.d: A small spill can be wiped up. It does not have to ruin the whole afternoon.

items.t: A clumsy rower blames the oar.
items.d: If a drawing looks messy, check your care before you blame the pencil.

items.t: Better healthy with little than rich and unwell.
items.d: Feeling well enough to play can matter more than a pile of extra toys.

items.t: Little streams join to form a great river.
items.d: Each classmate brings a few sticks. Together they can build a big fort.

items.t: A good start makes a job much easier to finish.
items.d: Begin well and the rest of the work gets easier.

items.t: Don't say 'up' before you have jumped.
items.d: Don't celebrate before you have really done it.

items.t: Whoever waits will get there.
items.d: Patience pays off. Good things can take time.

items.t: Not everything that shines is gold.
items.d: Something can look great outside but not be so special inside.

items.t: Whoever chases two hares catches neither.
items.d: Pick one goal at a time and you are more likely to reach it.

items.t: Listen more and talk less.
items.d: When you listen, you learn more about people and ideas.

items.t: Don't buy a cat in a bag.
items.d: Check something first before you pick it. Look inside the bag!

items.t: Nothing is too hard for someone who truly wants it.
items.d: When you really care, you find a way to do hard things.

items.t: No work, no cakes.
items.d: Nice rewards come from effort. To enjoy a cake, someone has to bake it.

items.t: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
items.d: Do your homework now and you'll have free time later.

items.t: A good name is the best inheritance.
items.d: Being known as honest and kind is worth more than money.

items.t: A fly does not fly into a closed mouth.
items.d: Sometimes saying less keeps you out of trouble.

items.t: The apple does not fall far from the tree.
items.d: Children often grow up a lot like their family.

items.t: Better a little than nothing.
items.d: A small bit is still worth having. Be glad for what you get.

items.t: It is easier to pull together in twos.
items.d: Teamwork makes heavy jobs lighter.

items.t: Still water wears away the banks.
items.d: Quiet people can be strong and deep thinkers.

items.t: A sparrow in the hand is better than a pigeon on the branch.
items.d: Keep what you have for sure instead of chasing something bigger.

items.t: Iron is forged while it is hot.
items.d: Act at the right moment, when the time is just right.

items.t: Whoever rises early grabs two pieces of luck.
items.d: Starting your day early gives you more chances.

items.t: There is no fire without smoke.
items.d: If you see a sign, there is usually a reason behind it.

items.t: Repetition is the mother of knowledge.
items.d: Practice over and over helps you remember, like times tables.

items.t: The wise learn from another's mistake.
items.d: You can learn from what happens to others, so you don't need to make every mistake.

items.t: Don't make an elephant out of a mosquito.
items.d: Don't blow a tiny problem up into a huge one.

items.t: A bird is known by its feathers, a person by their friends.
items.d: The friends you pick say a lot about you.

items.t: Drop by drop a pool forms.
items.d: Little bits add up. Saving a coin each day becomes a lot.

items.t: A lie has short legs.
items.d: Lies don't get far. The truth catches up quickly.

items.t: A friend is known in need.
items.d: A true friend helps you when you need help.

items.t: Slowly, you go further.
items.d: Steady, calm steps can take you farther than rushing.

items.t: Don't judge a book by its cover.
items.d: Get to know someone or something before you decide about it.

items.t: More heads, more sense.
items.d: Many minds together come up with better ideas.

items.t: After every storm comes the sun.
items.d: Hard times end, and good days come back.

items.t: No learning without effort.
items.d: To learn something new you have to work at it.

items.t: The morning shows how the day will go.
items.d: A good start to the day can set a happy mood.

items.t: Rush and you'll make people laugh.
items.d: If you hurry, you make silly mistakes.

items.t: Without effort you can't even pull a fish from a pond.
items.d: Even easy things need some work.

items.t: Live a century, learn a century.
items.d: You can keep learning your whole life.

items.t: Fear has big eyes.
items.d: Things seem scarier than they really are when you worry.

items.t: Four eyes see more than two.
items.d: Two people looking together notice more than one.

items.t: Like father, like son.
items.d: Children often learn habits and skills by watching their parents.

items.t: Every beginning is weak.
items.d: New skills may feel hard at first. Practice helps them grow stronger.

items.t: A mountain never meets a mountain, but a person meets a person.
items.d: People may cross paths again, so treat everyone well.

items.t: A fool's money is not long in his pocket.
items.d: Think before spending, or your money may quickly disappear.

items.t: Things are not as they seem.
items.d: Look closely and learn more before deciding what something is like.

items.t: Reason does not come before years.
items.d: Good judgment grows as we learn from time and experience.

items.t: A good word never broke a tooth.
items.d: Kind words cost nothing and can brighten someone's day.

items.t: The shoemaker goes barefoot.
items.d: People sometimes forget to use their own skills to help themselves.

items.t: Do not change horses in midstream.
items.d: When a careful plan is working, changing it halfway can cause trouble.

items.t: A rolling stone gathers no moss.
items.d: Someone who is always moving may not build lasting roots or routines.

items.t: Whoever would lead, let them be a bridge.
items.d: A good leader helps people connect and move forward together.

items.t: Whoever would be healthy, let them be cheerful.
items.d: A cheerful outlook can be one helpful part of feeling well.

items.t: A person is known by the friends they keep.
items.d: Choose friends who encourage kindness and good choices.

items.t: A rotten apple spoils the others.
items.d: One bad influence can spread through a group if nobody speaks up.

items.t: A good aunt is a second mother.
items.d: A caring aunt can offer family, help, and guidance.

items.t: Time is the healer.
items.d: Some hurt feelings become easier to manage as time passes.

items.t: Patience is the mother of all wisdom.
items.d: Waiting calmly gives you time to think and make wiser choices.

items.t: Hope is a safe anchor.
items.d: Hope can help you stay steady when life feels uncertain.

items.t: When the cat is away, the mice play.
items.d: Some people ignore rules when the person in charge is gone.

items.t: What is gained cheaply goes quickly.
items.d: We may value and protect something more when we worked for it.

items.t: Whoever farms the land will have plenty.
items.d: Patient work can produce useful rewards, like caring for a garden.

items.t: Whoever reflects should remember.
items.d: Think about past lessons and keep them in mind for next time.

items.t: Profit rarely comes without a venture.
items.d: Gaining something may require a thoughtful try and a little risk.

items.t: A close mouth catches no flies.
items.d: Sometimes staying quiet keeps you from saying something unwise.

items.t: As the old rooster crows, the young rooster learns.
items.d: Young people learn by copying what older people do.

items.t: Eagles catch no flies.
items.d: Do not waste your effort on tiny matters that do not deserve it.

items.t: Empty barrels make the most noise.
items.d: The loudest person is not always the one who knows the most.

items.t: Good health is better than wealth.
items.d: Having money matters less if you cannot enjoy a healthy life.

items.t: If you like the nut, crack it.
items.d: If you want a reward, be ready to do the work needed to reach it.

items.t: In at one ear and out at the other.
items.d: Hearing words is not enough. Pay attention and remember them.

items.t: It is a poor mouse that has only one hole.
items.d: It is wise to have another plan in case the first one fails.

items.t: Who cannot do as they wish must do as they can.
items.d: When the perfect choice is unavailable, do your best with what you have.

items.t: Delays are dangerous.
items.d: Putting off an important job can make it harder later.

items.t: Anger begins with foolishness and ends with regret.
items.d: Pause before acting in anger, or you may wish you had chosen differently.

items.t: Good goods make a quick market.
items.d: Things made well are often easier to trade or sell.

items.t: Old age should have honor.
items.d: Older people deserve respect for their years and experience.

items.t: It is not the cow that calls most that gives most milk.
items.d: The person who talks most may not be the one who does the most.

items.t: None is so deaf as the one who will not hear.
items.d: Advice cannot help someone who refuses to listen.

items.t: The smaller the group, the better the share. The bigger the group, the merrier the play.
items.d: Small groups may share more, while large groups can bring more fun.

items.t: A contented mind does not lack comfort.
items.d: Noticing what is good in your life can help you feel peaceful.

items.t: There is no flood that will not go down.
items.d: Hard times do not last forever. Problems can become smaller with time.

items.t: Listen to the wind on the hill until the waters go down.
items.d: When conditions are difficult, wait calmly for a safer time to act.

items.t: Understand the boat, and the boat will understand you.
items.d: Learn how your tools work, and you will use them with greater skill.

items.t: Well begun is half done
items.d: Starting well makes the rest easier. Lay out your pencils first, and the drawing goes better.

items.t: A bad workman quarrels with his tools
items.d: Blaming your pencil does not fix a messy page. Check how you are working, then try again.

items.t: Don't burn the candle at both ends
items.d: Do not work all day and all night. Rest helps you do better work tomorrow.

items.t: Don't bite off more than you can chew
items.d: Do not take on a job that is too big. Choose one chapter, not the whole book in one night.

items.t: The day is short and the work is long
items.d: There is a lot to do and the day ends. Start early so you are not rushing at bedtime.

items.t: If you want a thing done right, do it yourself
items.d: If the work matters, you may need to do it. A group poster still needs you to check every part.

items.t: Easier said than done
items.d: Talking about a job is simple. Doing it takes more care, like keeping your room tidy all week.

items.t: Shoemaker, stick to your last
items.d: A last is the foot-shaped form a shoemaker uses. The saying means stick to the work you know well.

items.t: Early to bed and early to rise, makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise
items.d: Sleeping and waking at steady times can help your body and your learning. A rested mind studies better.

items.t: Constant dropping wears away the stone
items.d: Tiny water drops can wear down a stone. Small practice, day after day, can crack a hard problem.

items.t: If at first you don't succeed, try, try again
items.d: A miss is not the end. Try once more, like tying a knot until it holds.

items.t: First things first
items.d: Do the most important job before the extra ones. Finish the homework, then play the game.

items.t: Experience is the best teacher
items.d: You learn most by trying. Reading about riding a bike is not the same as pedaling.

items.t: It's easy to be wise after the event
items.d: After a mistake, the better choice looks obvious. Next time, use what you noticed.

items.t: Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime
items.d: A gift helps once. A skill helps again and again. Learning to cook beats being handed one snack.

items.t: Forewarned, forearmed
items.d: Forewarned means told ahead. Forearmed means ready. If you know a test is coming, you can study.

items.t: He who hesitates is lost
items.d: Waiting too long can mean you miss your chance. Sign up for the team before the list is full.

items.t: If you're in a hole, stop digging
items.d: When a plan is going wrong, stop and change it. Do not keep adding to the mess.

items.t: It's never too late to mend
items.d: You can fix a mistake at any time. Apologize, or redo the page, even days later.

items.t: It's no use crying over spilt milk
items.d: Spilt means spilled. Do not stay upset about a mess you cannot undo. Clean it up and start again.

items.t: Never do things by halves
items.d: If you start a job, finish it properly. A half-done puzzle is not really done.

items.t: Measure twice, cut once
items.d: Check your numbers before you cut paper or wood. Measuring again can save the whole piece.

items.t: Don't have too many irons in the fire
items.d: Too many jobs at once means none gets your best. Finish one craft before starting three more.

items.t: The longest mile is the last mile home
items.d: The last part of a job can feel the hardest. Keep going, because the finish line is close.

items.t: If a job is worth doing, it is worth doing well
items.d: If a job is worth starting, give it your care. A sloppy map does not help anyone find the way.

items.t: Use it or lose it
items.d: Skills fade if you never practice. A language you skip all summer gets rusty.

items.t: Knowledge is power
items.d: Knowing things lets you make better choices. A reader has more ways to solve a problem.

items.t: Learning is the eye of the mind
items.d: Learning helps you notice what is really there. Study is like a light for your mind.

items.t: Hope for the best, prepare for the worst
items.d: Stay hopeful, and also make a backup plan. Pack a raincoat even when you hope for sun.

items.t: Many things are lost for want of asking
items.d: Want of means lack of. You miss good answers when you never ask. A question can save a lot of guessing.

items.t: Patience is a virtue
items.d: A virtue is a good habit of character. Patience means you can wait and keep trying without giving up.

items.t: Where there is a will there is a way
items.d: If you really want to learn something, you can find a path. Ask, practice, and try a new way.

items.t: Time and tide wait for no man
items.d: Time keeps moving and will not wait for you. Use today's hour, because it does not come back.

items.t: Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today
items.d: Do today's work today. A small task left until tomorrow often grows into a bigger one.

items.t: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
items.d: A true friend helps you when things are hard, not only when it is fun.

items.t: Our friends are our mirrors and show us ourselves.
items.d: Friends help us see what we are like, the good parts and the parts to grow.

items.t: Perfect friendship cannot be without equality.
items.d: Good friends treat each other as equals. Nobody is the boss of the friendship.

items.t: A man is known by the company he keeps.
items.d: The friends you choose say a lot about you, so pick friends who are kind.

items.t: Better to be alone than in bad company.
items.d: It is better to spend time by yourself than with people who treat others badly.

items.t: Two is a company; three is a crowd.
items.d: Sometimes two people want time alone. It is kind to notice and not push in.

items.t: Absence makes the heart grow fonder.
items.d: When we are away from people we love, we miss them even more.

items.t: A hedge between keeps friends green.
items.d: A little space and respect for privacy can keep a friendship fresh and happy.

items.t: Whoever gossips to you will gossip of you.
items.d: If someone says unkind things about others to you, they may say unkind things about you too.

items.t: Blood is thicker than water.
items.d: This saying means family ties can be very strong, so relatives often look after one another.

items.t: Charity begins at home.
items.d: Being kind starts with the people closest to us, like family and neighbours.

items.t: Home is where the heart is.
items.d: A home is about the people you love, not only the building.

items.t: Don't judge a man until you have walked a mile in his boots.
items.d: Try to imagine how it feels to be in someone else's place before you decide about them.

items.t: Fair play's a jewel.
items.d: Playing fairly is precious. It makes games and friendships better for everyone.

items.t: Give credit where credit is due.
items.d: When someone does a good job or has a good idea, say so and thank them.

items.t: Two wrongs don't make a right.
items.d: If someone is unkind, being unkind back does not fix anything.

items.t: Don't bite the hand that feeds you.
items.d: Be thankful to people who help you, and do not be rude to them.

items.t: Deal gently with the bird you mean to catch.
items.d: Gentle words and kind actions work better than being rough or pushy.

items.t: Kindness, like grain, increases by sowing.
