items.d: Plant kindness like seeds. The more you give, the more it grows all around.

items.t: Live and let live.
items.d: Respect how other people choose to live, and ask them to respect your choices too.

items.t: You can catch more flies with a drop of honey than with a barrel of vinegar.
items.d: Sweet, kind words get you much further than sour, angry ones.

items.t: Forgive and forget.
items.d: Let go of old arguments so you can be friends again and feel lighter.

items.t: Give and take is fair play.
items.d: In a good friendship, both people share and both people give way sometimes.

items.t: One hand washes the other.
items.d: When people help each other, everyone benefits. Helping is a two-way street.

items.t: Mind your P's and Q's.
items.d: Remember to be polite, with good manners like please and thank you.

items.t: Never look a gift horse in the mouth.
items.d: When someone gives you a present, be happy and thankful instead of finding faults.

items.t: Example is better than correction.
items.d: Showing kind behaviour teaches more than telling people what to do.

items.t: Who chases two rabbits catches neither.
items.d: Give one important goal your full attention.

items.t: A bat in a village without birds.
items.d: A weaker person may look important when better people are absent.

items.t: Wisdom from age is better than a tortoise shell.
items.d: Experience can teach lessons that take time to learn.

items.t: The smart hawk hides its talons.
items.d: Truly skilled people do not need to show off.

items.t: A leaving bird does not leave a mess.
items.d: Clean up after yourself before you go.

items.t: You cannot catch a tiger cub without entering its cave.
items.d: Reaching a big goal may require a brave first step.

items.t: When the tree falls, the monkeys scatter.
items.d: Some followers disappear when a leader loses influence.

items.t: One who rides a tiger is afraid to get off.
items.d: Think before starting something that may be hard to stop.

items.t: Catching crabs on a mountain is difficult.
items.d: This kind of job does not fit the place, so it will not work.

items.t: Teaching someone to fish is better than giving one fish.
items.d: A useful skill can help a person again and again.

items.t: Pluck a feather from every passing goose, but follow none completely.
items.d: Listen to many ideas, then think and choose for yourself.

items.t: The dogs bark, but the caravan passes on.
items.d: Do not let every complaint stop your progress.

items.t: At night all cats are gray.
items.d: When details are hidden, different things may look alike.

items.t: The bird loves her own nest.
items.d: People often feel a special love for their own home.

items.t: A bird is known by its song, and a person by their words.
items.d: What you say helps others understand your character.

items.t: Each sheep with its mate.
items.d: People with shared interests often enjoy being together.

items.t: A cat's child hunts mice.
items.d: Children often learn habits and skills from their families.

items.t: Flies do not enter a closed mouth.
items.d: Pausing before you speak can keep you out of trouble.

items.t: One who does not know the falcon roasts it.
items.d: Learn an object's value before deciding what to do with it.

items.t: When there are too many herders, the sheep get lost.
items.d: A job becomes confusing when too many people try to lead it.

items.t: Follow the bees and you may eat honey.
items.d: Look for helpful clues that can guide you toward a reward.

items.t: A leopard skin is beautiful to see, but inside there is an enemy.
items.d: A pretty outside does not tell you everything about what is inside.

items.t: If you make yourself honey, flies will overwhelm you.
items.d: Kindness is good, but it is also healthy to set limits.

items.t: The wolf feeds on its feet.
items.d: Effort and action often bring results, not waiting for luck.

items.t: A magpie brought the news on its tail.
items.d: This playful saying means that news came from an unnamed source.

items.t: The cat knows whose meat it has eaten.
items.d: A guilty person may reveal the truth through their behavior.

items.t: When the cat is away, the mice will play.
items.d: Some people ignore rules when the person in charge is gone.

items.t: A goose is not a pig's friend.
items.d: Those with very different interests may not easily get along.

items.t: The bird is known by its flight.
items.d: Actions show what someone can do better than boasts do.

items.t: A barking dog does not bite.
items.d: A person making loud threats may not take real action.

items.t: Birds hear daytime words, and rats hear nighttime words.
items.d: Speak carefully because someone may overhear you.

items.t: After three years at school, even a dog can recite a poem.
items.d: Time spent around learning can teach you a great deal.

items.t: Regret is too late after the birds have eaten the field.
items.d: Act in time instead of wishing later that you had acted sooner.

items.t: Who saw the peacock dance in the forest?
items.d: Wonderful work may go unnoticed if nobody can see or share it.

items.t: A monkey cannot know the taste of ginger.
items.d: It is hard to value something you do not understand.

items.t: Old foxes are hard to trap.
items.d: Experience helps people notice tricks and avoid mistakes.

items.t: Do not carry owls to Athens.
items.d: There is little use bringing something to a place that has plenty already.

items.t: A fish stinks from the head.
items.d: When a group has problems, its leaders may be the place to start looking.

items.t: One swallow does not make a summer.
items.d: One clue is not enough to prove that a larger change has happened.

items.t: Do not harness the oxen behind the wagon.
items.d: Do each step in the right order.

items.t: Who sleeps catches no fish.
items.d: You need to get started if you want results.

items.t: There is an eel under the rock.
items.d: Something about the situation may be hidden.

items.t: A bird fears a curved branch.
items.d: A bad experience can make someone cautious when a similar thing appears.

items.t: Sweet honey catches flies.
items.d: Gentle words often work better than harsh ones.

items.t: One grub can spoil the pot of soup.
items.d: One harmful part can affect the whole group or project.

items.t: The branches that grow the most fruit hang the lowest.
items.d: People who do a lot are often humble, like a full branch bending down.

items.t: Plow the field deep while others sleep, and you will have grain to spare.
items.d: Farmers who start early bring in more food. Starting early helps schoolwork too.

items.t: Praise the day at sunset.
items.d: Wait until the day is over before you call it good. The morning can still change.

items.t: Drop by drop, water wears away a stone.
items.d: One drip looks like nothing. Day after day, drips can carve a mark in rock.

items.t: You know the tree by its fruit.
items.d: Look at what a tree grows. You learn about people from what they do, too.

items.t: Make hay while the sun shines.
items.d: Hay must dry in the sun. When a good chance comes, use it before it passes.

items.t: Never cast off a warm coat till May is out.
items.d: Do not pack warm clothes away too early. Spring weather can still turn cold.

items.t: Kindness, like grain, grows when you sow it.
items.d: One planted seed can grow many grains. A kind act can spread in the same way.

items.t: The grass is always greener on the other side.
items.d: Another person's yard can look better from far away. Up close, it has weeds too.

items.t: Water can float a boat, and it can also sink it.
items.d: The same water can carry a boat or tip it over. Strong things can help or cause trouble.

items.t: The smell of plum blossom comes from the bitter cold.
items.d: Plum flowers open in the cold. A hard season can lead to something lovely.

items.t: If you do not plow, there will be no harvest.
items.d: Crops do not appear by themselves. If no one does the work, there is nothing to pick.

items.t: Ten years to grow a tree. A hundred years to raise a person.
items.d: Growing a tree takes years. Teaching a person well takes even longer.

items.t: A flower does not stay red for a hundred days.
items.d: Bright blooms fade. Happy times do not last forever, so enjoy them while they last.

items.t: Thick ice does not form in one cold day.
items.d: A frozen pond thickens night after night. Big things grow slowly.

items.t: A berry falls down by the roots of its tree.
items.d: Fruit lands near the plant it grew on. Children often take after their parents.

items.t: Many little strokes bring a large tree down.
items.d: Each small cut does little. Stay with the job, and a big tree can come down.

items.t: Three years on a rock.
items.d: If you can stay with a hard task for a long time, that patience can be worth it.

items.t: Let it wash away with the water.
items.d: Picture a leaf floating downstream. You can let a hurt feeling float away too.

items.t: If the river is noisy, it is carrying stones.
items.d: Rocks make the water loud. When there is a lot of talk, there is often a real cause.

items.t: A sun that rises too early does not last long.
items.d: Fruit that ripens too fast can spoil soon. Starting in a rush is not always best.

items.t: People meet one another, but the hills do not.
items.d: Hills stay in one place. People move about, so friends can meet again.

items.t: Even crooked wood can make a straight fire.
items.d: A bent log can still burn with a steady flame. Flaws do not stop all good work.

items.t: Patience brings roses.
items.d: Rose bushes take time. If you wait and keep caring for them, flowers can follow.

items.t: What you call into the woods comes back as an echo.
items.d: The forest sends your voice back. Kind words and mean words tend to come back too.

items.t: You leave the rain and stand under a dripping roof.
items.d: You get out of the storm, then drops still hit you. One problem can lead to another.

items.t: Still water turns stale.
items.d: A pond that never moves can start to smell. What we never use can go bad too.

items.t: Many small grains make a big heap.
items.d: One grain of wheat is tiny. Keep adding grains, and the pile becomes big.

items.t: Looking for wind in a field is a lost search.
items.d: You can feel wind, but you cannot catch it. This names a search that cannot work.

items.t: You can bend an alder tree little by little.
items.d: Slow, gentle pushing can change what force cannot. Patience works better than a hard shove.

items.t: Every vegetable has its time.
items.d: Beans, corn, and pumpkins each ripen in their own season. People grow in their time too.

items.t: Do not spit in a well. You may want the water later.
items.d: Keep the water clean even when you are not thirsty. Do not spoil what you may need.

items.t: In the rain no one fixes the roof. In sun, they forget the leak.
items.d: Wet tiles are hard to patch. On a dry day, it is easy to forget the drip.

items.t: After the rain comes fair weather.
items.d: Rain clouds move on. A stormy day can end in blue sky, and a hard day can too.

items.t: The sun can cross the mud and stay clean.
items.d: Sunlight shines on a muddy path and is not stained. You can pass a mess and stay kind.

items.t: Whatever you sow, you will reap.
items.d: Plant beans and you pick beans, not pears. Your actions come back like a crop.

items.t: Who has never felt the hot sun does not value the shade.
items.d: Shade feels wonderful after heat. Rest means more when you have worked hard.

items.t: Whoever loves the rose must bear its thorns.
items.d: A rose is lovely and it can prick. Many good things come with a hard part.

items.t: Time and tide wait for no one.
items.d: Time keeps moving and the sea will not wait for you. Use your time well.

items.t: Speak well of the highlands, but live in the lowlands.
items.d: The high hills are fine to praise. This saying chooses the gentler land for home.

items.t: Children always begin at the foundation.
items.d: Everyone starts with the basics. Strong learning grows from a strong start.

items.t: No kind deed has ever lacked its reward.
items.d: When you are kind, something good comes back to you in the end.

items.t: No cliff is so tall it cannot be climbed.
items.d: If you keep trying, even a very hard job can be done.

items.t: It takes a skillful sailor to go to Lehua.
items.d: Hard journeys need real skill, and skill comes from practice.

items.t: The awkward person breaks the board in riding on the surf.
items.d: Practice helps you gain the skill to avoid mistakes.

items.t: Love is far better than the poi dish or the fish bowl.
items.d: Food is good, but caring for each other matters even more.

items.t: Past the cliff, past the fears.
items.d: Once you get through the hard part, the worry can fade.

items.t: The eyes of a thief look every way.
items.d: Someone who is doing something sneaky keeps checking who is watching.

items.t: A small thing given with love.
items.d: It is not the size of a gift that counts. The love behind it does.

items.t: Love received demands love returned.
items.d: When someone is kind to you, be kind back.

items.t: Although it is small, it is a treasure.
items.d: Little things can be very special and valuable.

items.t: Unlike a canoe rope, a human bond cannot be cut.
items.d: The bonds between people can be very strong.

items.t: Goodwill towards others is a precious treasure.
items.d: Being kind and friendly to other people is precious.

items.t: Let us keep close together, not far apart.
items.d: Teams do better when they stay united.

items.t: Calm after the storm.
items.d: Hard times pass, and peaceful times come back.

items.t: Be a leader, not a follower.
items.d: Think for yourself and show others the way.

items.t: Caution is highly prized.
items.d: Being careful and thinking before you act is a great strength.

items.t: An active soul is a healthy soul.
items.d: Taking part in life can help your spirit feel well.

items.t: A problem is solved by continuing to find solutions.
items.d: Keep trying new ideas and you will work it out.

items.t: Some things are best left to work themselves out.
items.d: Sometimes patience is the best plan. Not every problem needs a push.

items.t: My precious jewel.
items.d: A loving way to call someone you treasure very much.

items.t: One family.
items.d: A Samoan saying about a group that belongs together as one family.

items.t: Like a canoe before the wind.
items.d: This Samoan saying describes anything that moves very fast.

items.t: This is under the chestnut tree.
items.d: In Samoa this means: this is a secret, so keep it quiet.

items.t: People do not own Country. Country owns them.
items.d: This means people belong to Country, rather than Country belonging to them.

items.t: Good stories can live for centuries.
items.d: People kept Aesop's fables alive by telling them aloud for generations.

items.t: An old story may have more than one storyteller.
items.d: Many fables were credited to Aesop even though he may not have created them all.

items.t: First, try to help yourself.
items.d: Before asking for help, make a real effort to solve the problem.

items.t: Working together can achieve what one cannot do alone.
items.d: A group can combine different ideas, skills, and strengths.

items.t: Get the facts before you act.
items.d: A little patience can stop a quick choice from becoming a regret.

items.t: Stories can cross borders and languages.
items.d: The Panchatantra grew into about 200 versions in more than 50 languages.

items.t: A helpful story can hide inside an animal tale.
items.d: The Panchatantra uses linked animal fables to share advice.

items.t: Friendship is worth learning how to build.
items.d: One Hitopadesha book is called How to Gain a Friend.

items.t: Friendship also needs care to last.
items.d: The Hitopadesha pairs a book about gaining friends with one about losing them.

items.t: Good advice can be passed from story to story.
items.d: Much of the Hitopadesha came from the older Panchatantra.

items.t: One hero can show a good quality in many forms.
items.d: In Jataka tales he may be a king or an animal and still teach that quality.

items.t: Warm care for others can be a story's lesson.
items.d: The Holy Swans story teaches that kind of care.

items.t: Tell the truth.
items.d: The Jataka story of Supaaraga teaches the value of truth.

items.t: A picture can keep an old story alive.
items.d: Hundreds of Jataka tales are shown at the Ananda Temple in Myanmar.

items.t: Searching in the easiest place may not find the answer.
items.d: Nasreddin looks outside for a ring lost indoors because the yard has more light.

items.t: Wisdom cannot be kept in one pot.
items.d: When Anansi's pot breaks, wisdom scatters everywhere for everyone.

items.t: Better bend than break.
items.d: Changing your plan can be wiser than holding firm out of pride.

items.t: Steady effort wins.
items.d: Keep making steady progress, even when someone else starts faster.

items.t: A person who often lies may not be believed later.
items.d: Trust is hard to rebuild, so tell the truth from the start.

items.t: No one is too small to help.
items.d: A small helper may have exactly the skill a bigger friend needs.

items.t: Kindness can come back to help you.
items.d: The lion's mercy is rewarded when the little mouse later helps him.

items.t: Work today to eat tomorrow.
items.d: Preparing early can make a future need easier to handle.

items.t: Greed can reach too far.
items.d: Trying to grab every reward can make you lose the good thing you already have.
items.a: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs

items.t: A simple, peaceful life can be better than uneasy luxury.
items.d: The country mouse chooses a plain bean over a fancy but troubled meal.
items.a: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse

items.t: Persuasion is better than force.
items.d: A warm, gentle approach can work when pushing harder does not.
items.a: The North Wind and the Sun

items.t: Thoughtfulness is stronger than brute strength.
items.d: A clever plan can solve a problem that force cannot.

items.t: Judge people by their actions, not their looks.
items.d: An impressive outside does not prove that someone behaves well.

items.t: Do not trade something real for a shadow.
items.d: Check that a tempting reward is real before giving up what you already hold.

items.t: Look at more than one side of a problem.
items.d: Each person in the elephant tale understands only the part they examine.

items.t: Clothes may hide a fool, but words give the truth away.
items.d: What you say and do shows more about you than a costume does.
items.a: The Ass in the Lion's Skin

items.t: Big promises can produce very little.
items.d: Strong results matter more than loud boasts about what will happen.

items.t: When everyone adds a little, everyone can share a lot.
items.d: In Stone Soup, each villager contributes an ingredient to make a meal together.

items.t: Which creature has one voice, but goes on four feet, then two, then three?
items.d: The Sphinx asked this old Greek riddle. The answer is a person.

items.t: Two sisters give birth to each other. Who are they?
items.d: Answer: day and night. Each one is followed by the other, again and again.

items.t: I neither know nor think I know.
items.d: Socrates said he did not pretend to know things he did not. Knowing what you don't know is where learning starts.

items.t: If you replace every plank of a ship, is it still the same ship?
items.d: The Greeks kept an old ship by swapping its rotted planks. Thinkers still argue about it.

items.t: Now build a second ship from the old planks. Which one is the real ship?
items.d: The thinker Thomas Hobbes added this twist in 1656. There is no simple answer.

items.t: Some books are to be tasted, others swallowed, and a few chewed and digested.
items.d: Some books you skim, some you read fast, and a few deserve slow, careful thought.

items.t: Teachers open the door. You enter by yourself.
items.d: A teacher can show you the way, but you must do the learning yourself.

items.t: Reading ten thousand books is not as useful as traveling ten thousand miles.
items.d: Books teach a lot, but seeing the world with your own eyes teaches even more.

items.t: Teaching someone to fish is better than giving them a fish.
items.d: A fish feeds you today. Knowing how to fish feeds you for life.

items.t: A small hole not mended in time becomes a big hole.
items.d: Fix little problems early. They get much harder to fix later.

items.t: The edge of a sword comes from sharpening.
items.d: Practice and hard work make you sharp, like a blade on a stone.

items.t: One who hears both sides is wise. One who hears only one side is in the dark.
items.d: Before you decide, listen to everyone. You will see more of the truth.

items.t: It is dark one inch ahead of you.
items.d: Nobody can see the future for sure. Plans can change.

items.t: Good medicine is bitter to the mouth.
items.d: Helpful advice can be hard to hear, but it is good for you.

items.t: A wise person hears one word and understands two.
items.d: Wise people listen closely and think about what is behind the words.

items.t: Still water digs deep.
items.d: Quiet people can think very deeply. You don't need to be loud to be wise.

items.t: Even silence speaks.
items.d: Not saying anything can tell a lot too. Listen to what quiet means.

items.t: Don't say it's wheat until you harvest it.
items.d: Wait until things are finished before you boast about them.

items.t: If the herders are many, the sheep get lost.
items.d: Too many bosses can make a mess. Teams need clear directions.

items.t: The first pancake is always a blob.
items.d: First tries are often messy. Don't give up, the next one gets better.

items.t: Live for a century, learn for a century.
items.d: You can keep learning your whole life. There is always more to discover.

items.t: Don't enter a river before you know where it is safe to cross.
items.d: Learn about something before you act.

items.t: Every why has its because.
items.d: A good question can lead to an explanation. Keep asking why and check what you find.

items.t: Any man can make a mistake, but only a fool keeps making the same one.
items.d: Learn from mistakes so you don't repeat them.

items.t: Second thoughts are best.
items.d: Thinking again often gives a better answer than your first idea.

items.t: By teaching, we learn.
items.d: When you explain something to someone, you understand it even better.

items.t: A drop hollows a stone by falling often, and a person grows wise by reading often.
items.d: Small steady efforts add up to big results over time.

items.t: One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.
items.d: Even when you work hard, you see what is left to do. Remember to notice how far you have come too!

items.t: We must have perseverance and above all confidence in ourselves.
items.d: Keep going when things are hard, and believe that you can do it.

items.t: I was taught that the way of progress was neither swift nor easy.
items.d: Getting better at something takes time and effort, and that is normal.

items.t: I am among those who think that science has great beauty.
items.d: Science is not just facts. Finding out how things work can feel as lovely as music or art.

items.t: I learned very early the difference between knowing the name of something and knowing something.
items.d: Knowing a bird's name is a start. Watching what it eats and how it flies is real knowing.

items.t: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.
items.d: Be honest with yourself, especially when you really want something to be true.

items.t: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
items.d: If you can build it or explain it yourself, you truly understand it.

items.t: I don't feel frightened by not knowing things.
items.d: It is fine not to know everything. Not knowing is where the fun of finding out begins.

items.t: We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
items.d: We are made from the universe, and when we study the stars, the universe is learning about itself.

items.t: The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff.
items.d: Many atoms in your body were made inside stars long ago.

items.t: If you wish to make an apple pie from scratch, you must first invent the universe.
items.d: Not every atom in a pie was made at the start. Stars made many of them later.

items.t: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.
items.d: If someone says something really amazing, ask for really good proof.

items.t: Imagination will often carry us to worlds that never were. But without it we go nowhere.
items.d: Dreaming up new ideas is the first step to every discovery.

items.t: A book is proof that humans are capable of working magic.
items.d: A book lets you hear the thoughts of someone you have never met, even from long ago.

items.t: Look again at that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us.
items.d: He was talking about a photo of Earth taken from far away, where our planet looks like a tiny dot.

items.t: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
items.d: He learned so much because people before him had already worked so hard. We build on each other.

items.t: I have no special talents. I am only passionately curious.
items.d: Wanting to know how things work can take you a very long way.

items.t: Imagination is more important than knowledge.
items.d: Facts are useful, but new ideas start when you imagine what could be.

items.t: The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existing.
items.d: Keep asking why. Being curious is good all by itself.

items.t: Life is like riding a bicycle. To keep your balance you must keep moving.
items.d: He wrote this to his son. Keep trying and keep going, and you stay steady.

items.t: The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious.
items.d: Things we do not understand yet are exciting, because they are waiting to be discovered.

items.t: It is possible to fly without motors, but not without knowledge and skill.
items.d: Before building a plane with an engine, the Wright brothers learned to fly gliders very carefully.

items.t: Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.
items.d: Amazing things can be real, as long as they follow the rules of how nature works.

items.t: Work, finish, publish.
items.d: His advice to a young scientist: do the work, finish it, then share it with the world.

items.t: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
items.d: We may not know the whole future, but there is lots of useful work we can start right now.

items.t: The world needs all kinds of minds.
items.d: People think in different ways, and every way of thinking can help the world.

items.t: Remember to look up at the stars and not down at your feet.
items.d: Stay curious about the big world around you, and keep wondering.

items.t: This is for everyone.
items.d: The inventor of the World Wide Web wanted it to be free for all people to use.

items.t: That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.
items.d: The first step on the Moon in 1969 was tiny for one person but huge for all people.

items.t: We choose to go to the Moon in this decade... not because they are easy, but because they are hard.
items.d: Doing hard things helps us grow and learn what we can really do.

items.t: The vast loneliness is awe-inspiring and it makes you realize just what you have back there on Earth.
items.d: Seeing Earth from the Moon showed him how special our home planet is.

items.t: Because it's there.
items.d: His answer when asked why he wanted to climb Mount Everest. Explorers love a big challenge.

items.t: The mountains are calling and I must go.
items.d: He loved nature so much that the wild places always pulled him outside to explore.

items.t: It is not half so important to know as to feel.
items.d: For children, loving and wondering about nature matters even more than learning its names.

items.t: The more that you read, the more things you will know. The more that you learn, the more places you'll go.
items.d: Reading opens doors to new ideas, new places and new adventures.

items.t: Today you are You, that is truer than true. There is no one alive who is Youer than You.
items.d: Nobody else is exactly like you, and that is something to celebrate.

items.t: You have brains in your head. You have feet in your shoes. You can steer yourself any direction you choose.
items.d: You can think for yourself and choose your own path.

items.t: Unless someone like you cares a whole awful lot, nothing is going to get better. It's not.
items.d: From The Lorax. If you care about something, like trees or animals, you can help it.

items.t: A person's a person, no matter how small.
items.d: Everyone matters, big or little, young or old.

items.t: Oh, the thinks you can think up if only you try!
items.d: Your imagination is full of ideas waiting for you to discover them.

items.t: I meant what I said and I said what I meant.
items.d: Horton the elephant keeps his promise. Being trustworthy means doing what you said you would.

items.t: You're off to Great Places! Today is your day! Your mountain is waiting, so... get on your way!
items.d: Big adventures start with a first step today.

items.t: If you have good thoughts they will shine out of your face like sunbeams and you will always look lovely.
items.d: Kind and happy thoughts show on your face and make you shine.

items.t: Those who don't believe in magic will never find it.
items.d: Stay open to wonder, and you will notice amazing things everywhere.

items.t: It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye.
items.d: From The Little Prince. The most important things, like love and friendship, you feel rather than see.

items.t: I am not afraid of storms, for I am learning how to sail my ship.
items.d: From Little Women. Hard times feel less scary when you are learning how to handle them.

items.t: Isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?
items.d: From Anne of Green Gables. Every morning is a fresh start.

items.t: All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us.
items.d: Gandalf says this in The Lord of the Rings. We cannot choose everything, but we choose what we do.

items.t: Not all those who wander are lost.
items.d: People who wander and explore may still know exactly where they are headed.

items.t: Why, sometimes I've believed as many as six impossible things before breakfast.
items.d: The White Queen in Through the Looking-Glass. Imagining impossible things is great practice for your mind.

items.t: Begin at the beginning, and go on till you come to the end: then stop.
items.d: From Alice in Wonderland. A simple plan for telling a story, or doing almost any job.

items.t: It's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
items.d: Alice says this. We grow and change every day.

items.t: You have been my friend. That in itself is a tremendous thing.
items.d: Charlotte the spider says this in Charlotte's Web. Friendship is a gift in itself.

items.t: There is nothing, absolutely nothing, half so much worth doing as simply messing about in boats.
items.d: Ratty says this in The Wind in the Willows. Simple fun outdoors is one of life's best things.

items.t: The world is so full of a number of things, I'm sure we should all be as happy as kings.
items.d: There are so many wonderful things to see and do. That is a good reason to be happy.

items.t: Just living is not enough... one must have sunshine, freedom, and a little flower.
items.d: A butterfly says this in his story. Small joys like sunshine and flowers make life sweet.

items.t: Two roads diverged in a wood, and I, I took the one less traveled by, and that has made all the difference.
items.d: In his poem, a traveler chooses one path and later feels that this choice mattered.

items.t: Anything can happen, child. Anything can be.
items.d: From a poem in Where the Sidewalk Ends. The future is full of possibilities.

items.t: Their names are What and Why and When and How and Where and Who.
items.d: Kipling said these six question words were his helpers that taught him all he knew.

items.t: Always do right. This will gratify some people and astonish the rest.
items.d: Doing the right thing makes people happy, and surprises the ones who did not expect it.

items.t: How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world.
items.d: You do not have to be grown up to help. You can start making things better right now.

items.t: Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement. Nothing can be done without hope and confidence.
items.d: Believing things can go well helps you work hard and reach your goals.

items.t: Life is either a daring adventure, or nothing.
items.d: She could not see or hear, yet she lived boldly. Try new things and be brave.

items.t: Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.
items.d: People face hard things, but people are also very good at getting through them.

items.t: Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.
items.d: Being mean back does not fix meanness. Kindness is what makes things better.

items.t: I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it.
items.d: Brave people still feel scared, but they do not let fear stop them.

items.t: One child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world.
items.d: She spoke at the United Nations about why every child should get to go to school.

items.t: You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
items.d: Trying something that feels too hard is how you find out you are stronger than you thought.

items.t: Never give in, never give in, never, never, never, never.
items.d: He said this to students at his old school. Keep trying, even when things are tough.

items.t: Always bear in mind that your own resolution to succeed is more important than any other one thing.
items.d: From a letter to a young man. Your own decision to keep trying matters most.

items.t: Far and away the best prize that life has to offer is the chance to work hard at work worth doing.
items.d: Working hard on something that really matters is one of the best feelings there is.

items.t: I cannot live without books.
items.d: He loved reading so much he wrote this in a letter to his friend John Adams.

items.t: Well done is better than well said.
items.d: Doing something is better than just talking about it.

items.t: Lost time is never found again.
items.d: Use your time well, because you cannot get it back.

items.t: Pressure is a privilege.
items.d: Feeling nervous before a big moment means you have earned a chance to do something special.

items.t: You can observe a lot by watching.
items.d: A funny way of saying: pay attention and you will learn a lot.

items.t: It ain't over till it's over.
items.d: Do not give up early. Things can still change before the end.

items.t: We don't make mistakes, just happy little accidents.
items.d: A painter's way of saying a mistake can turn into something new and nice.

items.t: There's no person in the whole world like you, and I like you just the way you are.
items.d: Mister Rogers told children on TV that each of them was special.

items.t: The Analytical Engine can do whatever we know how to order it to perform.
items.d: Computers need clear instructions. Learning to give them instructions is programming.

items.t: Every individual matters. Every individual has a role to play.
items.d: You are important, and you can find your own way to help.

items.t: Only if we understand can we care.
items.d: Learning about people, animals, and nature can help us care for them.

items.t: Only if we care will we help.
items.d: Caring can turn a kind thought into a useful action.

items.t: We humans are not so different from other animals as we used to think.
items.d: Careful study can reveal surprising connections between living things.

items.t: Humans are allergic to change.
items.d: Change can feel uncomfortable, but trying something new helps us grow.

items.t: You manage things, you lead people.
items.d: Good leaders listen, encourage, and help people work together.

items.t: I've always been more interested in the future than in the past.
items.d: She liked to look ahead and think about what people could build.

items.t: When anything went wrong with a computer, we said it had bugs in it.
items.d: Problems can get playful names. What matters is staying curious and fixing them.

items.t: Science and everyday life cannot and should not be separated.
items.d: Science is part of cooking, weather, health, light, sound, and much more.

items.t: We especially need imagination in science.
items.d: Discoveries begin when someone wonders, imagines, and asks a new question.

items.t: Science is imaginative, inspiring, uplifting.
items.d: Science can fill your mind with fresh ideas and a sense of wonder.

items.t: You are made of star stuff, and you are connected to the universe.
items.d: She meant that people are part of the universe around them.

items.t: It is easy to sleep while floating. It feels very comfortable.
items.d: Sally Ride said resting in space can feel cozy because you float.

items.t: From a mountaintop, stars look much brighter than at sea level.
items.d: Sally Ride means a high place can show you a brighter night sky.

items.t: In space, I felt very comfortable in the universe.
items.d: Mae Jemison said being in space felt comfortable, out in the universe.

items.t: I like to think of ideas as potential energy.
items.d: An idea is stored power. When you try it, that power can become action.

items.t: The arts and sciences are both expressions of human creativity.
items.d: A painting and a science question can both grow from a creative mind.

items.t: Never be limited by other people's limited imaginations.
items.d: If someone thinks your dream is too small, you can still imagine more.

items.t: If you have a dream, follow it.
items.d: A dream is the start. Kalpana Chawla means you then work to make it real.

items.t: The journey matters as much as the goal.
items.d: What you learn on the way can matter as much as the finish line.

items.t: The coolest thing was floating and not feeling my weight.
items.d: In space you float. Kalpana Chawla loved that light, free feeling.

items.t: Imagine a history teacher making history!
items.d: Christa McAuliffe meant a teacher can do something big enough to be history.

items.t: Reach for it. Push yourself as far as you can.
items.d: Try the hard thing. You may go farther than you first thought.

items.t: What are we doing here? We are reaching for the stars.
items.d: Christa McAuliffe meant exploring space is how people reach a bold dream.

items.t: May your future be limited only by your dreams!
items.d: She hoped kids would let big dreams, not small limits, shape their lives.

items.t: Do not waste the Earth. It is our jewel.
items.d: Buzz Aldrin called Earth a jewel and said we should take care of it.

items.t: Let's go!
items.d: Yuri Gagarin shouted 'Poyekhali' at launch. It means 'Let's go!'

items.t: Orbiting Earth, I saw how beautiful our planet is.
items.d: Yuri Gagarin wrote this after his flight. Earth looked wonderful from space.

items.t: What an amazing range of colors!
items.d: Yuri Gagarin said this about Earth from space. The colors were hard to describe.

items.t: "Preparation, I have often said, is rightly two-thirds of any venture."
items.d: Get ready well before you start. Packing and planning make the big day go smoothly.

items.t: "In soloing, as in other activities, it is far easier to start something than it is to finish it."
items.d: Starting is easy. The brave part is keeping going until you are done.

items.t: "Courage is the price that Life exacts for granting peace."
items.d: To feel calm and happy, you sometimes have to be brave first.

items.t: "We have seen new land to the South never seen by human eyes before."
items.d: He wrote this about an Antarctic march. Imagine being the first to see a place!

items.t: "Victory awaits him who has everything in order."
items.d: Careful planning, like checking your gear, helps you win. People just call it luck.

items.t: "Far and away the greatest threat to the sea and to the future of mankind is ignorance."
items.d: The more we learn about the ocean, the better we can look after it.

items.t: "Water, the blue, is the key to life."
items.d: All known life on Earth needs water.

items.t: "I am not a scientist. I am, rather, an impresario of scientists."
items.d: He said his job was to bring scientists together so they could explore the sea.

items.t: Shackleton's ship Endurance got trapped in thick sea ice in the Weddell Sea and later sank.
items.d: His crew had to find a new plan, and they never gave up.

items.t: Shackleton's crew had small lifeboats about 6 metres long. The strongest was named the James Caird.
items.d: It was tiny for a trip across a huge, stormy ocean.

items.t: Shackleton sailed a small boat to South Georgia to find help for his stranded crew.
items.d: He took action because his crew needed help.

items.t: Shackleton rescued all 22 men who were waiting for help on Elephant Island.
items.d: Every single one came home. That is great leadership.

items.t: Shackleton and three friends once got closer to the South Pole than anyone before them.
items.d: They reached 88°23' S. That is very near the bottom of the world.

items.t: Roald Amundsen's team was the first to reach the South Pole, on 14 December 1911.
items.d: They travelled across the ice on skis and with sled dogs.

items.t: Amundsen sailed the small ship Gjøa through the Northwest Passage, the first to do it.
items.d: The trip took from 1903 to 1906.

items.t: Roald Amundsen is known as the first person to reach both the South Pole and the North Pole.
items.d: He explored both ends of the Earth.

items.t: In 1926 Amundsen and his crew flew over the North Pole in an airship called Norge.
items.d: Exploring with a flying machine instead of a ship!

items.t: Amundsen's Maud expedition was strongly inspired by Fridtjof Nansen's earlier Arctic voyage.
items.d: Heroes can show us what is possible.

items.t: Jacques Cousteau helped invent the Aqua-Lung, the first successful open-circuit scuba gear.
items.d: It let divers breathe underwater and explore the sea freely.

items.t: Cousteau's ship Calypso was rented to him for just one franc a year.
items.d: That was a tiny price for a ship that explored the oceans.

items.t: Cousteau's ocean film The Silent World won the top prize at the 1956 Cannes Film Festival.
items.d: It also won an Academy Award for best documentary in 1957.

items.t: Cousteau led Conshelf experiments to test if people could live and work on the seafloor.
items.d: Imagine a home under the waves!

items.t: Jacques Cousteau started the Cousteau Society to help protect ocean life.
items.d: He wanted everyone to care for the sea.

items.t: In 1970 Sylvia Earle led the first all-female team of aquanauts in Tektite II.
items.d: They lived and worked underwater as a team.

items.t: Sylvia Earle dived near Oahu in a special suit, reaching about 381 metres deep.
items.d: That is deeper than most skyscrapers are tall.

items.t: Sylvia Earle was the first woman to be chief scientist of NOAA, from 1990 to 1992.
items.d: She helped lead NOAA's science work.

items.t: Sylvia Earle's group Mission Blue names Hope Spots, ocean places that matter for ocean health.
items.d: Hope Spots draw attention to places that are important to a healthy ocean.

items.t: Sylvia Earle has the nickname Her Deepness.
items.d: The nickname celebrates her work exploring the deep sea.

items.t: Before becoming a famous climber, Edmund Hillary worked as a beekeeper with his dad and brother.
items.d: Great adventurers can start with ordinary jobs.

items.t: On 29 May 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first confirmed to reach the top of Mount Everest.
items.d: They climbed it as a team.

items.t: In 1958 Hillary's team reached the South Pole overland, the first to use motor vehicles.
items.d: They crossed part of Antarctica in motor vehicles.

items.t: Hillary's Himalayan Trust helped build many schools and hospitals in Nepal.
items.d: The trust built places for learning and medical care.

items.t: Edmund Hillary was the first man to stand on both poles and on the top of Everest.
items.d: What a record for a beekeeper from New Zealand!

items.t: Tenzing Norgay worked as a high-altitude porter on three Everest trips before he reached the top.
items.d: He kept trying, and it paid off.

items.t: Tenzing Norgay became the first Director of Field Training at the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute.
items.d: He taught new climbers what he had learned.

items.t: Time magazine named Tenzing Norgay one of the 100 most influential people of the 20th century.
items.d: The honor recognized his influence.

items.t: In 1932 Amelia Earhart became the first woman to fly nonstop alone across the Atlantic Ocean.
items.d: She made the nonstop flight all by herself.

items.t: In 1928 Amelia Earhart was the first woman to cross the Atlantic Ocean by airplane.
items.d: She went as a passenger. Her big solo flight came four years later.

items.t: In 1935 Amelia Earhart was the first to fly solo from Honolulu, Hawaii, to Oakland, California.
items.d: She flew over a very wide stretch of ocean.

items.t: Amelia Earhart was the first woman to receive the Distinguished Flying Cross, in 1932.
items.d: It is an award for amazing flying.

items.t: Amelia Earhart was the first president of the Ninety-Nines, a group of women pilots.
items.d: She helped women pilots support each other.

items.t: On 1 September 1985 Robert Ballard's team found the wreck of the Titanic on the ocean floor.
items.d: The wreck lay deep beneath the sea.

items.t: Robert Ballard started the JASON Project to get students excited about science and technology.
items.d: The program helped middle school students learn about science and technology.

items.t: Robert Ballard leads ocean exploration on the research ship E/V Nautilus.
items.d: The ship helps scientists explore the deep sea.

items.t: In 1960 Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh reached the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench.
items.d: They went down in the bathyscaphe Trieste, about 10,916 metres deep.

items.t: Jacques Piccard's father, Auguste, was an adventurer too. Their family set height and depth records.
items.d: Adventure can run in the family.

items.t: Ranulph Fiennes was the first person to visit both the North Pole and the South Pole by surface travel.
items.d: He travelled on the ground and ice, not by plane.

items.t: In 1993 Ranulph Fiennes and Mike Stroud crossed Antarctica unsupported in 93 days.
items.d: They made the journey without outside support.

items.t: "You can't be a writer if you're not a reader."
items.d: Reading fills your mind with words, ideas, and ways to tell stories.

items.t: "It's the great writers who teach us how to write."
items.d: Reading excellent books can help you grow as a writer.

items.t: "Story helps us to understand and live creatively with change."
items.d: When life changes, stories can help us imagine new ways forward.

items.t: "I can't imagine a man really enjoying a book and reading it only once."
items.d: A favorite book may reveal something new each time you return.

items.t: "Friendship is the greatest of worldly goods."
items.d: A caring friend can be worth more than anything you can buy.

items.t: "Some day you will be old enough to start reading fairy tales again."
items.d: Wonder and imagination are worth keeping as you grow.

items.t: "The reading makes all real woods a little enchanted."
items.d: A story can make an ordinary walk feel full of possibilities.

items.t: "Piglet took Pooh's arm."
items.d: A small, caring action can tell a friend, "I am here with you."

items.t: "I just wanted to be sure of you."
items.d: Good friends remind each other that they are not alone.

items.t: "I've got a sort of idea, but I don't suppose it's a very good one."
items.d: Share a new idea, even before it feels perfect.

items.t: "It's the best way to write poetry, letting things come."
items.d: Sometimes a poem begins by patiently noticing the words that arrive.

items.t: "It is the best means they have for taming Wild Things."
items.d: Sendak meant that fantasy helps children explore big feelings through stories.

items.t: "Children are tough."
items.d: Children can meet challenges and keep growing.

items.t: "We have the power to imagine better."
items.d: Picture how something could improve, then take one small step toward it.

items.t: "Above all, watch with glittering eyes the whole world around you."
items.d: Look closely and eagerly. Ordinary places can hold amazing details.

items.t: "It doesn't matter who you are or what you look like, so long as somebody loves you."
items.d: Being loved and cared for matters far more than looking a certain way.

items.t: "Hold fast to dreams."
items.d: Keep your hopes close, especially while you work toward them.

items.t: "Poems are like rainbows. They escape you quickly."
items.d: When a bright poem appears, write it down before it slips away.

items.t: "I used to half believe and wholly play with fairies when I was a child."
items.d: You can enter an imaginary game fully while knowing it is pretend.

items.t: The most certain way to succeed is always to try just one more time.
items.d: If you feel like quitting, try once more. That one more try might be the one that works.

items.t: To invent, you need a good imagination and a pile of junk.
items.d: Great ideas start in your head. Old bits and pieces can become something new.

items.t: I find out what the world needs. Then, I go ahead and invent it.
items.d: Edison looked for problems people had, then worked to solve them.

items.t: Genius is one per cent inspiration, ninety-nine per cent perspiration.
items.d: Perspiration means sweat. Big ideas need lots of hard work to come true.

items.t: Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.
items.d: Bell wrote these as the first words spoken over his telephone, on 10 March 1876, to his helper.

items.t: You cannot force ideas. Successful ideas are the result of slow growth.
items.d: Good ideas need time to grow, like a plant. Be patient with your thinking.

items.t: Before everything else, getting ready is the secret of success.
items.d: Preparing well, like packing your bag the night before, helps you do your best.

items.t: Thinking is the hardest work there is.
items.d: Good thinking takes real effort, just like exercise. Practise it every day.

items.t: Nothing is particularly hard if you subdivide it into small jobs.
items.d: A big task feels easier when you do it one small step at a time.

items.t: Money is only a tool in business.
items.d: Ford meant money can help a business do its work, like any other tool.

items.t: Wisdom is the daughter of experience.
items.d: Leonardo wrote that we become wise by trying things and learning from them.

items.t: Every instrument requires to be made by experience.
items.d: Leonardo meant that to build good tools, you must test and learn by doing.

items.t: Mechanics is the paradise of the mathematical sciences.
items.d: This means math can help explain how machines, gears, and levers work.

items.t: The Book of the science of Mechanics must precede the Book of useful inventions.
items.d: First learn how things work. Then you can invent useful things.

items.t: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.
items.d: Steve Jobs said this to students. If you have not found what you love yet, keep looking.

items.t: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life.
items.d: Jobs meant you should follow your own interests and not just copy others.

items.t: You can't connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backwards.
items.d: What you learn today may help you in ways you cannot see yet.

items.t: Stay hungry. Stay foolish.
items.d: Jobs ended a speech with this borrowed line. It means keep learning and dare to try.

items.t: Be alone, that is the secret of invention; be alone, that is when ideas are born.
items.d: Tesla found quiet time helped him think. Try a quiet moment to dream up ideas.

items.t: His duty is to lay the foundation for those who are to come, and point the way.
items.d: Tesla meant that scientists should help future scientists build on their work.

items.t: Let the future tell the truth and evaluate each one according to his work.
items.d: Tesla believed people should be remembered for what they actually do.

items.t: Please cut off a nanosecond and send it over to me.
items.d: Hopper used a short wire to show how far a signal could travel in one nanosecond.

items.t: I think things that work well start to look good as well.
items.d: Dyson, an inventor, said a well-made tool often looks great too.

items.t: It was a simple machine that changed my life.
items.d: Kamkwamba said this about a windmill he built from old parts.

items.t: Whatever happens, don't give up.
items.d: Kamkwamba built a windmill from old parts. His advice is to keep going.

items.t: If you love what you do and are willing to do what it takes, it's within your reach.
items.d: Wozniak, a computer inventor, says love and hard work can put big goals within reach.

items.t: I wanted my own computer my whole life.
items.d: Wozniak dreamed for years of having a computer of his own.

items.t: “Four million different solutions to the problems of staying alive.”
items.d: Living things survive in many amazing ways.

items.t: “As far as we know, the Earth is the only place in the universe where there is life.”
items.d: Our living planet is precious and worth caring for.

items.t: “Neither we nor any other animal can survive without plants.”
items.d: Plants provide food and help make the air we breathe.

items.t: “We destroy plants at our peril.”
items.d: Protecting plants also protects people and animals.

items.t: “The time has now come for us to cherish our green inheritance, not to pillage it.”
items.d: Care for the natural world passed down to us.

items.t: “With skill and care and knowledge, we can ensure that there is still a place on Earth for birds.”
items.d: Learning about birds can help us protect their homes.

items.t: “Our faculties are more fitted to recognize the wonderful structure of a beetle than a Universe.”
items.d: Start your curiosity with the small wonders you can observe.

items.t: “The pleasure of observing and reasoning was a much higher one than that of skill and sport.”
items.d: Looking closely and thinking carefully can bring great joy.

items.t: “I became interested in them, and wished to learn how far they acted consciously.”
items.d: Even ordinary earthworms can inspire important questions.

items.t: “The subject may appear an insignificant one, but we shall see that it possesses some interest.”
items.d: A small or ordinary subject may hold surprising discoveries.

items.t: “The best instruction is that which uses the least words sufficient for the task.”
items.d: A clear lesson says just enough to help someone begin.

items.t: “To stimulate life, leaving it free, however, to unfold itself, that is the first duty of the educator.”
items.d: A teacher can spark learning while giving a child room to grow.

items.t: “The children are the makers of men.”
items.d: What children learn and practice helps shape the adults they become.

items.t: “The child is truly a miraculous being.”
items.d: Every child has a remarkable power to learn and grow.

items.t: “The adult must find within himself the still unknown error that prevents him from seeing the child as he is.”
items.d: Adults should question their own ideas and listen carefully to children.

items.t: “Always look for the helpers.”
items.d: When something is difficult, notice the people offering care and support.

items.t: “Everybody longs to be loved, and longs to know that he or she is lovable.”
items.d: Kind words can remind people that they matter.

items.t: “We just don't get to be competent human beings without a lot of different investments from others.”
items.d: Many people help us learn, grow and become capable.

items.t: “Children are to be respected and I respect them deeply.”
items.d: A child's ideas and feelings deserve careful attention.

items.t: “I give an expression of care every day to each child, to help him realize that he is unique.”
items.d: Regular kindness helps children see what is special in themselves.

items.t: “Our job in life is to help people realize how rare and valuable each one of us really is.”
items.d: Help others notice their own worth and strengths.

items.t: “The best way to lift one's self up is to help someone else.”
items.d: Helping another person can make both of you stronger.

items.t: “Few things can help an individual more than to place responsibility on him.”
items.d: Being trusted with a real task helps you grow.

items.t: “Nothing ever comes to me, that is worth having, except as the result of hard work.”
items.d: Valuable goals often need patience and steady effort.

items.t: “There is as much dignity in tilling a field as in writing a poem.”
items.d: Useful work deserves respect, whether it uses hands or words.

items.t: “Character, not circumstances, makes the man.”
items.d: Your choices and actions help show who you are.

items.t: “The world cares a great deal about what you or I do.”
items.d: What you do can matter more than what you know.

items.t: “Don't look for big things, just do small things with great love.”
items.d: A tiny caring act can make an ordinary day better.

items.t: “The hunger for love is much more difficult to remove than the hunger for bread.”
items.d: People need care and belonging as well as food.

items.t: “Civilization is a method of living, an attitude of equal respect for all men.”
items.d: A good community treats every person with respect.

items.t: “You don't need a diploma to plant a tree.”
items.d: You can take a useful step without being an expert.

items.t: “Trees are living symbols of peace and hope.”
items.d: Planting and caring for a tree can show hope for the future.

items.t: “Restore the home of the tadpoles.”
items.d: Protecting a small pond can protect many living things.

items.t: “Give back to our children a world of beauty and wonder.”
items.d: Care for nature so future children can enjoy and explore it.

items.t: “Until you dig a hole, you plant a tree, you water it and make it survive, you haven't done a thing.”
items.d: Good ideas matter most when you turn them into action.

items.t: “The best way to find yourself is to lose yourself in the service of others.”
items.d: Helping people can teach you what you value and what you can do.

items.t: “If we could change ourselves, the tendencies in the world would also change.”
items.d: Improving your own habits can influence the people around you.

items.t: “The only tired I was, was tired of giving in.”
items.d: Determination can help you stand firm for what you know is right.

items.t: “I did not get on the bus to get arrested. I got on the bus to go home.”
items.d: An ordinary moment can reveal someone's quiet courage.

items.t: “Every individual matters. Every individual has a role to play. Every individual makes a difference.”
items.d: Each person is important and can help the world in some way.

items.t: “Only if we understand can we care. Only if we care will we help.”
items.d: Learning about living things can inspire us to protect them.

items.t: “When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the Universe.”
items.d: Nature is connected, so a change in one place can affect another.

items.t: “None of Nature's landscapes are ugly so long as they are wild.”
items.d: Wild places have their own beauty, even when they look rough or untidy.

items.t: Gravity pulls things toward Earth.
items.d: When you drop a sock, gravity pulls it to the floor.

items.t: Friction can slow things that slide.
items.d: A book pushed across a table slows down as it rubs against the table.

items.t: Moving things tend to keep moving.
items.d: When the car stops, your seat belt stops you from moving forward.

items.t: The same push speeds up a light cart more than a heavy cart.
items.d: With an equal push, an empty shopping cart speeds up faster than a full one.

items.t: A push is met by an equal push in the other direction.
items.d: Push water backward with your hands as you swim. The water pushes you forward.

items.t: Light bounces off a mirror.
items.d: When you brush your teeth, light from your face bounces off the mirror into your eyes.

items.t: Light can bend when it goes from water into air.
items.d: A straw in a clear glass of water can look bent at the water line.

items.t: Sounds start with something shaking back and forth.
items.d: Pluck a guitar string and watch it shake as it makes a sound.

items.t: Faster shaking makes a higher note.
items.d: On a guitar, pressing a string closer to the bridge leaves less string to shake and makes a higher note.

items.t: Heat moves from warmer things to cooler things.
items.d: A metal spoon warms up when you leave it in hot soup.

items.t: Water pushes upward on things in it.
items.d: A beach ball pops up when you let it go underwater.

items.t: A push farther from a pivot can turn something more easily.
items.d: A door swings open more easily when you push near the handle than when you push near the hinges.

items.t: Two north poles of magnets push each other away.
items.d: Bring the north ends of two toy bar magnets together and feel them push apart.

items.t: Electric current needs a complete path to keep flowing in a simple circuit.
items.d: A flashlight switch breaks the path when you turn it off.

items.t: Rubbing materials together can build up an electric charge.
items.d: Rub a balloon on your hair. The balloon can then pull your hair toward it.

items.t: A feather and a hammer fall together when there is no air.
items.d: Astronauts showed this on the Moon. On Earth, air slows the feather.

items.t: Air pushes against things moving through it. This is air resistance.
items.d: You feel it push on your face when you ride a bike fast.

items.t: A parachute has a big surface, so air slows its fall a lot.
items.d: The wide cloth catches lots of air, so the jumper drifts down gently.

items.t: Flat paper falls slower than the same paper crumpled into a ball.
items.d: The flat sheet catches more air, so air pushes up on it more.

items.t: A streamlined shape slides through air more easily.
items.d: Cyclists crouch low and wear smooth helmets to cut through the wind.

items.t: Weight is the pull of gravity on an object.
items.d: You weigh less on the Moon because the Moon pulls more gently.

items.t: Mass is how much stuff is in something. It stays the same everywhere.
items.d: A bag of flour holds the same amount of flour on Earth or the Moon.

items.t: Rough surfaces make more friction than smooth ones.
items.d: Sandpaper grips your hand more than a smooth sheet of plastic.

items.t: Friction turns movement into heat.
items.d: Rub your hands together fast and they get warm.

items.t: Wet ice has very little friction, so things slide easily.
items.d: Ice skates glide, but your shoes slip on a wet icy path.

items.t: A force is a push or a pull.
items.d: You push a swing. You pull a wagon.

items.t: Unbalanced forces change how something moves.
items.d: A bigger pull from one team drags the rope and the other team.

items.t: A rocket moves up by pushing hot gas down.
items.d: A balloon zooms the other way when you let its air rush out.

items.t: When you jump off a skateboard, the board rolls backward.
items.d: Your push on the board is matched by its push on you.

items.t: A pendulum swings back and forth with a steady beat.
items.d: A playground swing takes about the same time for each swing.

items.t: A longer pendulum swings more slowly.
items.d: A swing on long chains takes longer per swing than one on short chains.

items.t: Something moving in a circle keeps changing direction.
items.d: A car going around a roundabout is always turning, even at steady speed.

items.t: Speed tells how far something goes in a set time.
items.d: A bike going 10 km in one hour has a speed of 10 km per hour.

items.t: A ball thrown sideways still falls at the same time as one dropped.
items.d: Both hit the ground together, but the thrown one lands farther away.

items.t: A ball thrown in an arc follows a curved path.
items.d: A basketball shot rises, slows, then curves down into the hoop.

items.t: Pressure is a push spread over an area.
items.d: The same push on a small spot presses harder than on a big spot.

items.t: A sharp knife cuts better because its edge is very thin.
items.d: All your push goes onto a tiny edge, so the pressure is high.

items.t: Water pressure gets bigger the deeper you go.
items.d: Your ears can feel it when you dive to the bottom of a pool.

items.t: Air has weight, and it pushes on everything around us.
items.d: A sealed bag of chips looks puffy up a mountain because outside air pushes less.

items.t: A drinking straw works because air pushes on the drink.
items.d: You make low pressure in the straw and the air pushes juice up.

items.t: A heavy ship floats because it is shaped to hold lots of air.
items.d: Its wide hollow shape pushes aside enough water to hold it up.

items.t: Something floats if it is less dense than the liquid.
items.d: A cork floats in water because it is lighter for its size.

items.t: Light travels in straight lines.
items.d: Sunbeams through a gap in the curtains look like straight streaks.

items.t: A shadow forms when something blocks light.
items.d: Stand in sunshine and your body blocks the light behind you.

items.t: Light moves much faster than sound.
items.d: You see lightning first and hear the thunder a little later.

items.t: Clear things let light through. Opaque things block light.
items.d: You can see through a window, but not through a wooden door.

items.t: A white light can split into a rainbow of colors.
items.d: A glass prism or raindrops can bend each color a different amount.

items.t: A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through raindrops.
items.d: The drops bend the light and spread it into colors.

items.t: A red apple looks red because it bounces red light to your eyes.
items.d: It soaks up most other colors of light that hit it.

items.t: Dark clothes get warmer in the sun than light clothes.
items.d: A black T-shirt feels hotter than a white one on a sunny day.

items.t: A smooth mirror shows a clear picture, but rough surfaces do not.
items.d: Still water works like a mirror, but a rippled pond does not.

items.t: A magnifying glass is a curved piece of glass that bends light.
items.d: It makes small things like ants look bigger.

items.t: Your eyes see because light bounces off things and enters them.
items.d: In a completely dark room, you cannot see anything at all.

items.t: Sound travels as waves of vibration through air.
items.d: Shout across a field and the air carries the shaking to a friend.

items.t: Sound cannot travel through empty space.
items.d: With no air to shake, space is silent.

items.t: Sound travels faster through water than through air.
items.d: Underwater, you can hear a splash from a long way off.

items.t: Sound travels through solid things too.
items.d: Put your ear on a table and tap the far end. It sounds louder.

items.t: An echo is sound that bounces off a hard surface.
items.d: Shout in a tunnel or an empty hall and your voice comes back.

items.t: A bigger vibration makes a louder sound.
items.d: Hit a drum hard and the skin shakes more, so it is louder.

items.t: Metal is a good conductor of heat. Heat moves through it quickly.
items.d: A metal spoon in hot soup soon feels hot at the handle.

items.t: Wood and plastic are poor conductors of heat.
items.d: Pot handles are plastic or wood so they stay cooler to hold.

items.t: Insulation slows down heat moving from place to place.
items.d: A woolly hat keeps your body heat from escaping.

items.t: Trapped air is a great insulator.
items.d: A puffy coat is warm because tiny pockets of air hold your heat in.

items.t: A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot or cold by slowing heat transfer.
items.d: Its double walls have almost no air between them to carry heat.

items.t: Metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature.
items.d: It pulls heat from your hand faster, so your skin feels cold.

items.t: Warm air rises, and cool air sinks.
items.d: The air near the ceiling of a room is warmer than near the floor.

items.t: Heat can travel as rays you feel, without touching.
items.d: You feel warmth from a campfire or the Sun on your face.

items.t: Most things get bigger when heated and smaller when cooled.
items.d: Bridges have small gaps so they can stretch safely in hot weather.

items.t: A liquid thermometer works because the liquid in it expands when it warms.
items.d: The liquid rises up the thin tube as the temperature goes up.

items.t: Heat is energy moving, and temperature tells how hot something is.
items.d: A bathtub of warm water stores more energy than a cup at the same temperature.

items.t: Water takes a long time to heat up and cool down.
items.d: The sea stays cool on a hot day, and the sand gets very hot.

items.t: Moving things have movement energy, called kinetic energy.
items.d: A fast rolling ball can knock over more skittles than a slow one.

items.t: Things held up high have stored energy from gravity.
items.d: A child at the top of a slide has stored energy that turns into motion.

items.t: A stretched rubber band stores energy.
items.d: Let go of it and it zips across the room.

items.t: Food gives your body stored energy to move and grow.
items.d: A good breakfast gives you energy to run around at break time.

items.t: Plants store energy from sunlight in their leaves and food.
items.d: Sunlight helps plants grow, and animals get energy by eating them.

items.t: A battery stores energy ready to turn into light, sound or motion.
items.d: A torch turns battery energy into light.

items.t: A bouncing ball loses a little energy each bounce.
items.d: Some turns into sound and heat, so it bounces lower each time.

items.t: Solar panels turn light from the Sun into electricity.
items.d: Some calculators run on a small solar panel with no battery.

items.t: A wind turbine turns the movement of wind into electricity.
items.d: The wind spins the blades and a generator makes power.

items.t: A bulb in a circuit lights up when current passes through it.
items.d: A torch lights only when the switch completes the path.

items.t: Metals like copper let electricity flow easily. They are conductors.
items.d: Wires are made of copper, with a plastic cover around them.

items.t: Rubber and plastic do not let electricity flow. They are insulators.
items.d: The plastic coating on a charger cable keeps the electricity inside.

items.t: A magnet pulls on iron and steel, but not on wood or plastic.
items.d: A fridge magnet clings to the steel door, but not to a wooden shelf.

items.t: The Earth acts like a giant magnet.
items.d: A compass needle lines up with Earth's magnetic field and points north.

items.t: A magnet has two ends called poles, a north and a south.
items.d: If you cut a magnet in half, each piece has both poles.

items.t: A magnet's push or pull works through paper and thin plastic.
items.d: A magnet can move a paper clip across a table from underneath.

items.t: Opposite electric charges attract. Matching charges push apart.
items.d: Hair stands up after a balloon rub because the strands push each other.

items.t: A lever turns around a fixed point, called a fulcrum.
items.d: A seesaw turns on its middle so one end goes up as the other goes down.

items.t: A longer lever lets you lift a heavy thing with a smaller push.
items.d: A long crowbar can pry up a heavy lid more easily than a short one.

items.t: A wheelbarrow is a lever that helps you carry heavy loads.
items.d: Lifting the handles takes less effort than lifting the load by hand.

items.t: A ramp lets you raise something with less force, over a longer path.
items.d: It is easier to push a box up a slope than to lift it straight up.

items.t: A screw is a ramp wrapped around a pole.
items.d: It turns and pulls itself into wood, going down a tiny slope.

items.t: A wedge is two ramps joined together.
items.d: An axe or a knife splits things apart by pushing sideways as it goes in.

items.t: A pulley uses a rope and wheel to change the direction of a pull.
items.d: A flag goes up when you pull the rope down.

items.t: Gears are wheels with teeth that turn each other.
items.d: On a bike, the gears help you pedal up steep hills.

items.t: Simple machines make a job easier, but they do not give free energy.
items.d: A ramp needs less push, but you must push over a longer distance.

items.t: Things are steadier with a low center of gravity.
items.d: A tall, narrow stack of books tips over more easily than a wide pile.

items.t: The center of gravity is the point where an object balances.
items.d: A ruler balances on your finger at its middle.

items.t: A wide base makes things hard to tip over.
items.d: A traffic cone sits steadily on its wide square bottom.

items.t: Bending your knees helps you stay balanced.
items.d: On a skateboard you crouch to keep your weight low and steady.

items.t: A longer stopping time means a smaller force.
items.d: Bending your knees when you land from a jump makes the landing softer.

items.t: An elastic thing springs back to its shape after being stretched.
items.d: A trampoline stretches down and then pushes you back up.

items.t: Lightning is a huge spark of static electricity.
items.d: It is like the spark you may see taking off a woolly jumper, but much bigger.

items.t: Tires have treads, grooves that help them grip the road.
items.d: Even on a wet road, the grooves help the tire hold on.

items.t: Wide snowshoes stop you sinking into snow.
items.d: Your weight spreads over a big area, so the pressure is smaller.

items.t: Oil floats on water because it is less dense.
items.d: Oil drops in soup gather on top instead of mixing in.

items.t: Salty water pushes up harder than fresh water.
items.d: It feels easier to float in the sea than in a swimming pool.

items.t: A hot air balloon rises because hot air is lighter than cool air.
items.d: The warm air inside is less dense than the cool air outside.

items.t: Fill glasses with different amounts of water to make different notes.
items.d: Tap a glass with more water and the note sounds lower.

items.t: Soft things soak up sound.
items.d: A room with thick curtains and rugs sounds quieter than an empty room.

items.t: A big drum makes a deeper sound than a small drum.
items.d: A bass drum goes boom, while a little drum goes tap.

items.t: A shadow is longest when the Sun is low in the sky.
items.d: Your shadow is very long in the late afternoon.

items.t: A wheel on an axle rolls with less friction than sliding.
items.d: A trolley with wheels is easier to push than a box dragged on the floor.

items.t: Archimedes explained the upward push on things in a fluid.
items.d: A boat floats when the water it pushes aside weighs as much as the boat.

items.t: A lever can help a small push move something heavy. A seesaw is a lever.
items.d: Archimedes is credited with saying: "Give me a place to stand on, and I will move the Earth."

items.t: Galileo built telescopes that could magnify up to about 30 times.
items.d: Magnify means to make something look bigger than it really is.

items.t: Galileo discovered Jupiter's four largest moons.
items.d: He saw four small companions that travel along with the giant planet.

items.t: Galileo showed that Venus has phases, just like our Moon.
items.d: Venus can look like a thin crescent or a round bright disk.

items.t: Galileo worked out that mountains and craters make the Moon's shadow edge uneven.
items.d: Tall mountains and crater rims catch sunlight, so the line between light and dark looks bumpy.

items.t: Galileo is said to have watched a swinging lamp and learned about pendulums.
items.d: A playground swing is a pendulum. Small swings take nearly the same time each way.

items.t: Galileo first thought Saturn's rings were extra planets.
items.d: What looked like nearby planets was really a ring around Saturn.

items.t: Galileo studied sunspots, dark patches on the Sun.
items.d: A telescope helped him study those dark spots in more detail.

items.t: Johannes Kepler found laws for how planets move.
items.d: The laws describe the paths planets take as they travel through space.

items.t: Kepler worked in Prague as assistant to astronomer Tycho Brahe.
items.d: He helped Brahe study the sky and the moving planets.

items.t: Kepler wrote Somnium, an early story about a trip to the Moon.
items.d: Because of that story, he is called a father of science fiction.

items.t: At age six, Kepler watched the Great Comet of 1577.
items.d: A comet can look like a fuzzy star with a long glowing tail.

items.t: Schoolboy Isaac Newton built sundials and model windmills.
items.d: A sundial tells time with a shadow. A model windmill shows how wind can push.

items.t: Newton and Gottfried Leibniz both get credit for calculus.
items.d: Calculus is math about change, like how fast a ball speeds up as it falls.

items.t: In 1687 Newton published laws of motion and universal gravity.
items.d: The same pull that drops a ball also keeps the Moon near Earth.

items.t: Newton showed that a prism splits white light into colors.
items.d: You see the same colors when sunlight makes a rainbow in the sky.

items.t: Newton built a working telescope that used a mirror, not a big lens, to collect light.
items.d: Light bounces off the mirror, and faraway things look closer.

items.t: At age 26, Newton became Lucasian Professor at Cambridge.
items.d: The full title is Lucasian Professor of Mathematics.

items.t: Faraday used a magnet and electricity to make a wire spin.
items.d: Electric motors in fans and toy cars use this spinning idea.

items.t: Moving a magnet through a wire loop makes an electric current.
items.d: Faraday found this. Generators use it to make the electricity in homes.

items.t: At 14, Faraday began training as a bookbinder.
items.d: An apprentice learns a job by working with a skilled person.

items.t: Faraday gave Christmas science lectures for young people.
items.d: He gave them at the Royal Institution so children could hear real science.

items.t: Faraday filled soap bubbles with gases to test magnets.
items.d: A bubble can float. He watched whether a magnet pulled the gas inside.

items.t: Faraday showed a metal cage can keep electricity outside.
items.d: In 1836 he stood inside a charged metal mesh. This shield is called a Faraday cage.

items.t: The farad, a unit for how much charge a part can store, honors Faraday.
items.d: This ability is called capacitance. A capacitor is a part that stores electric charge.

items.t: Faraday's first battery used seven British halfpenny coins.
items.d: The coins were part of his first recorded science experiment.
